I reviewed the desktop shell of the frozen snapshot (electron/main.cjs, preload.cjs, lib.cjs, src/platform, desktopIntegration.ts, the io open/recent/save/autosave files, the index.html CSP and the package.json build config). Most of the hardening is sound. The repo's own check script (52 checks) passes against my scratch copy. The path allowlist (grants) has no bypass with Windows path forms: alternate data streams, trailing dots/spaces, 8.3 names, \\?\ and \\.\ prefixes, `..` and case/slash variants are all refused or resolve to the same file. The main-thread file:// filter blocks traversal, `%2e%2e`, encoded `\`, UNC hosts, `file:////`, `C|`, sibling-prefix folders and drive variants. IPC sender checks still work after a crash and reload. Fonts and lazy chunks load from an asar inside a folder whose name has spaces and accented letters. A bad document cannot crash-loop the app at launch: recovery waits for the user, and files from the command line are delivered only once.

Six findings:
1. Major, security: a Worker inside the page can read any local file. Worker loads never reach the main-process filter, so the documented file sandbox can be bypassed. Fixing the CSP to `worker-src 'none'` stops it and still passes all 52 checks in `--full` mode.
2. Major, data loss: choosing "Quit Anyway" in the native fallback prompt deletes the autosave recovery data, even though that prompt says autosave may recover the work.
3. Major, workflow: a .pgfx dropped onto the window opens with no file path. Save then asks where to save (Save As, with no folder pre-filled), and dropping a project that is already open creates a second copy.
4. Minor: a `%` anywhere in the install path makes the filter block the app's own index.html, so the window stays blank.
5. Minor: the packaged app obeys the `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL` environment variable. It loads whatever URL that names and gives the page the full desktop bridge.
6. Minor, from reading the code only (I could not test it on Windows): the page fully controls the Save dialog's default path and file extensions. A network-share path there should make Windows contact that server when the dialog opens, which can leak the user's Windows login hash.

Not reported: I could not check whether Roblox's servers allow the avatar lookup from the app, because the network proxy blocks roblox.com.

**1. Minimal repro (v1-psd-glow.mjs)**
- Setup: 800x600 document with background #ece8df, a #222 rectangle, and an outer glow (#ff1f1f, opacity 0.35, size 40, blend mode Screen). Screen is the effect's default blend mode (glows.ts:26).
- Export: File ▸ Export as PSD through the real dialog. "Bake" is ticked by default, and the dialog note says "...so the PSD looks exactly like your document." Then reopen the PSD.

- Bake OFF: 0 pixels differ.
- The export toast is a plain "Exported PSD (165 KB)" with no warning.

**2. Real flow (v1-look-psd.mjs tpl-gothic-paper crimson-film)**
- Steps: Gothic Paper template, then a click on the Crimson Film card in the Looks panel, then a default PSD export.
- Bake ON: 84,299 pixels differ, maxDiff 99, and a red halo is clearly visible around the hair and shoulders (shots/look-tpl-gothic-paper-crimson-film-sidebyside.png).
- Bake OFF: maxDiff 5.

**3. Rasterize Layer Style (v1-rasterize-glow.mjs)**
- Running layer.rasterizeStyle on the minimal document changes the image by the same 50,820 px / maxDiff 69.
- There is no warning, although the doc comment says it bakes "without changing the image".

**Root cause**
- The renderer draws each behind-stage effect onto the backdrop with its own blend mode (engine.ts:1796-1800, compositeRender).
- `renderLayerToDoc` → `flattenRender` (engine.ts:2654-2665) draws those pieces onto a transparent canvas instead. Screen or Multiply over transparent pixels is just Normal.
- psd.ts:266/280 bakes through this path. layerOps.ts:1241-1244 (bakeStyle) flattens the same way. Its split branch at :1250 also merges every behind effect into one Normal "Effects" layer.
- HANDOFF lines 142-143 only mention non-Normal *layer* blend modes for Rasterize, not effect blend modes. So this is not a known gap.

**Scope, for calibrating severity** (v1-templates-psd.mjs runs all 13 templates unmodified)
- The visible error needs a coloured Screen glow or Multiply shadow over a mid-tone or light backdrop. A white Screen glow and a black Multiply shadow (the defaults) come out identical.
- Templates as shipped show at most 31 levels of difference (simulator-bright 31, update-banner 16), which is barely visible.
- Templates with a top-level Vignette show 0 composite difference. The baked Vignette is an opaque full-canvas pixel layer that hides everything below it, so the halo is still in the character layer but is covered. My sunburst + Sunburst Halftone run is diff 0 for exactly this reason.
- The shipped Looks, Styler styles and effect presets add coloured Screen glows (red, amber, green, cyan, purple, pink). Gothic Paper, one of the headline styles, has no Vignette, so the halo shows as soon as one of these is applied to it.
- I'd keep this at **major**: it is the default option, the dialog promises an exact match, the output is silently wrong, and it shows in a headline flow. It is not a blocker, because .pgfx and PNG output are exact and unticking Bake gives a correct PSD.

**On the proposed fix**
- The primary suggestion ("bake Normal effects, write non-Normal ones natively") is wrong.
  - Photoshop computes a native outer glow or drop shadow from the layer's pixel alpha. That alpha would then include the baked stroke or Normal shadow, so the glow would wrap the stroke. Our renderer computes it from the content alone.
  - It also defeats the reason people tick Bake: GIMP and other apps that ignore layer styles.
- The reviewer's fallback is the right fix: one pixel layer per effect, carrying that effect's blend mode. This is the same idea as Photoshop's Layer Style ▸ Create Layers. See betterFix for the details.
verdict.betterFix:
Split the layer the same way compositeRender draws it, rather than flattening it.

1. **Export the renderer's split.** Add `renderLayerParts(doc, layer, {mask})` to src/render/compositor.ts. It wraps the internal `renderLayer` and returns `{ behind: {canvas, op}[], core }` in document space, which is exactly what compositeRender draws. HANDOFF already lists this as a pending request.

2. **Use it in psd.ts `buildPsd`** when `bake` is on and any enabled behind-stage effect has a blend mode other than Normal (or the layer's own blend is non-Normal):
   - Write each behind piece, in order, as its own pixel layer directly below the content layer.
   - Name it `"<layer> <Effect name>"`. Set its `blendMode` to the piece's blend (via `toPsdBlend` of the effect's `params.blendMode`) and its opacity to the layer's opacity.
   - Copy the layer's `hidden`, `clipping` and mask to it. Alternatively, render it with `mask: true` and leave the PSD mask off.
   - Write the core (content plus above-stage effects) as the main layer with the layer's own blend and opacity.
   - This matches compositeRender step for step: each piece is drawn at `globalAlpha = l.opacity` with its own op, then the core with the layer's blend. Consecutive Normal pieces can be merged into one layer.
   - Add a toast note, e.g. "glows/shadows exported as separate layers: …".

3. **Do the same in `bakeStyle`** (src/panels/layerOps.ts:1224):
   - If any behind effect is not Normal, always take the split branch.
   - Emit one raster layer per behind effect, with `blendMode = effect.params.blendMode`, using the existing `renderAlone` + `unknockAlpha` logic per effect, instead of a single Normal "Effects" layer.

4. **Add tests:**
   - An outer glow (Screen, #ff1f1f) over a light fill, exported with `bakeStyles: true` and composited back, should be within 2–3 levels of `renderDocument`.
   - The same check for `rasterizeStyleSelected`.

5. **Fix the dialog text** at PsdExportDialog.tsx:33 so it stays accurate.

confirmed.title: Dragging the template character re-runs all its smart filters on every mouse move (about 3 fps on 1080p templates)
confirmed.issue: After Replace Character, the next thing a user does is drag the character into place. The renderer only reuses a layer's previous render when the layer has no smart filters, mask or position-dependent effects. Every template character carries smart filters (gradient-map + halftone, or cel-shade) and usually a glow. So every pointermove of a plain Move-tool drag re-runs those filters and the glow at full resolution. Even pixel-local filters such as gradient-map, which give the same result wherever the layer sits, are re-run. This is not the known per-filter speed item: the filters are re-run although only the layer's position changed.

- smart filters, glow removed: 286 / 278
- glow only: 129 / –

confirmed.fix: Let translationSig accept layers whose smart filters don't depend on position: gradient-map, curves, levels, hue/sat and the other pixel-local adjustments, plus filters anchored to the layer rather than the document. Give each filter definition a translation-safe flag. For filters anchored to the document (halftone grid), reuse the previous render shifted by the whole-pixel offset while a move or nudge is in progress, mark it approximate, and re-render after the drag ends. The existing settle mechanism used after paint strokes can do that re-render. Benchmark the Crimson drag before and after with f21b-drag-profile.mjs.

Reproduced on the snapshot build (snap-dist served on port 5393). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-e2e-flows-v2/v1-drag-filters.mjs. It wraps every registered filter's apply() to count calls and time them, then does 20 real Move-tool mouse moves of 6 px on the character.

Code: src/render/engine.ts:750 makes translationSig() return null whenever the layer has an enabled smart filter. So on every pointermove of a plain drag (move.ts calls preview() per move), the character is rebuilt from scratch: content redrawn, filter stack run, outer glow recomputed. This is not mentioned in HANDOFF; only a comment in the code says so.

Measured on this box (shared 2.1 GHz Xeon), ms per pointermove:
- Crimson as shipped, GPU (SwiftShader): 217-225. Same with filters removed, glow kept: 74. With nothing on the layer: 67. Software canvas: 210 vs 82.
- Crimson after Replace Character (studio.png): 225 vs 86.
- Gothic (cel-shade only): 91-109 vs 37.
- Per move, halftone runs once at full resolution (920x1132, about 80 ms) and gradient-map once (4-6 ms). There are also tiny thumbnail calls.
- The cost is not only the filter time. On Crimson with just gradient-map (2.6 ms) plus the glow, a move costs 132 ms on the software canvas vs 82 ms, because the glow and content get rebuilt as well.
- Crimson drags at about 4.5 fps here, not the "about 3 fps" reported (that box was busier). Real desktop hardware should be roughly twice as fast, which is still choppy on the main action after opening a template.

Overstatement: not every template character has smart filters. Gothic, Sunburst (cel-shade) and Crimson (gradient-map + halftone) do, plus three extra templates (cel-shade, rim-light). The others use only stroke, glow or shadow effects, and those already take the shift path. Characters styled with the Character Styler (rim-light and similar filters) are also affected.

Major is defensible: it is a performance problem only (output is correct and the drag ends in the right place), but it is in the most common post-template action, and the fix is cheap and exact for most templates.

Validated the exact part of the fix: in a scratch copy (rv-e2e-flows-v2/proto/src/render/engine.ts:750-752), allowed cel-shade and non-dither adjustment filters, and added the filter identity to the signature.
- Gothic: 109 -> 39.5 ms per move.
- Crimson with gradient-map + glow: 123 -> 77 ms per move.

verdict.betterFix:
1) Exact path (covers Gothic, Sunburst, the cel-shade and rim-light extras, and Styler filters):
- Give filters a docAnchored flag, mirroring EffectMeta.docAnchored. Mark the filters that read ctx.offsetX/offsetY or call anchor(ctx) (halftone, comic-dots, vignette, grain, scanlines, ...).
- In translationSig (src/render/engine.ts:747-751), return null only when an enabled filter is doc-anchored, instead of rejecting every hasFilters() layer.
- Do not limit this to pixel-local filters. Neighborhood filters that never read the offset (cel-shade, rim-light, blurs) give the same result when the render is shifted by whole pixels. The existing need/clip check already handles content clipped at the document edge.
- Add `|f${objId(l.filters)}` to the returned signature. Today it leaves filters out because filtered layers never reach that line. Without it, a filter edit could reuse a stale shifted render.
- Filters whose output depends on where the crop starts need extra care. Gradient-map's dither uses x&3 / y&3 measured from the region's corner. For these, allow the shift only when a fresh render's region would equal the shifted base region (layer not clipped by the document edge), or when dx and dy are multiples of the 16 px alignGrid.

2) Doc-anchored filters (Crimson's halftone):
- While a move preview is still uncommitted (move tool / nudge), let only live composites (rc.approxOk) reuse the shifted previous render. Mark it approximate (moved.approx = true; markApprox(rc, l.id, moved.region)), like the existing approx-base branch in renderLayer.
- The existing settle (SETTLE_MS) then re-renders it exactly about 350 ms after the drag stops. renderDocument, exports and thumbnails already skip approximate renders.
- Side effect: the dots move with the character during the drag and snap back to the document grid when it settles. That matches Photoshop's behaviour for smart objects.

Benchmark with v1-drag-filters.mjs (shipped / fxonly modes, GPU and SWCANVAS=1). Check exactness the way v2-diff.mjs does: export after the drag and compare with a build that renders from scratch.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch on the snapshot build (snap-dist, port 5394, software canvas) with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-e2e-flows-v3/v-look-target.mjs. Logs are in out-noir-*.txt and out-glitch-*.txt, exports in exports/, screenshot in shots/Noir_Newspaper-text.png.

Observed:
1) Crimson template. Select the "Name" text layer, set Looks to Layer and click Noir Newspaper. The toast reads 'Applied look "Noir Newspaper" to "Name"…', yet 99.99% of pixels change, and mean chroma drops from 45.7 to 0: the whole thumbnail turns grayscale and gets the clippings. The tree shows a root "Look: Noir Newspaper" group (Levels, Black & White, Halftone, Clippings), and the drop shadow lands on Name.
2) With the character active, Layer mode and Document mode give byte-identical exports (md5 15f36402… for both).
3) This identical output only happens for looks with no document-scope layerFilters. Glitch Signal does differ: Layer mode puts glitch and chromatic-aberration as smart filters on the character, while Document mode adds a Glitch adjustment layer. By code, Vaporwave, Cyber Neon, Retro Print and Glitch Signal differ. The other 18 of 22 looks are a no-op toggle in the default state, because templates open with the character selected and the stored mode defaults to 'layer' (src/looks/store.ts:22,41).

Why I rate it minor, not major: this is intended behaviour, not a code defect. The engine contract (src/looks/engine.ts:11-17, insertLookDraft :527-544) says overlays and adjustments always go in a root "Look:" group. The Tips text (src/ui/shell/TipsDialog.tsx:106) calls a Look a "cohesive style" and says "Select your character layer first to stylize it". The target only chooses where filters and effects go and which layer anchors the 'behind' atmosphere. Live card previews, on by default, render the full-document result for the current target before you click (LooksPanel.tsx:140, preview.ts). The apply is one undo step, and the main flow (template, character, look) gives the intended result. What is genuinely misleading is the wording. The toggle has aria-label "Apply looks to" with options Layer/Document. The Layer tooltip ("filters and effects go on the active layer", LooksPanel.tsx:312) leaves out that grades and textures cover everything. The toast says "to "Name"" (engine.ts:659). For most looks the toggle does nothing. That is confusing polish, not wrong output.

The proposed main fix is wrong as a default. Clipping or confining the look group to the target in Layer mode would break the primary flow: Layer is the default mode and the character is preselected, so every look would grade only the character. The background would stay red and un-noired, the opposite of the reference styles. It would also contradict the documented contract. Only the reviewer's "at minimum" option (fix the copy) is right.

Side observation, outside this finding: on the Name text the look's drop shadow stacks on the template's own drop shadow (fx=drop-shadow+drop-shadow). adoptTemplateStylingDraft only adopts on placeholder layers (characterStyling.ts:241), so same-type effects on non-character targets are never replaced.
verdict.betterFix:
Keep the engine as it is and fix the copy so it matches the design.
(a) Rename the segmented control's meaning from scope to subject. Set aria-label to "Look subject" and label the options "Active layer" and "Auto (character)", or keep the labels and change the tooltips. Layer tooltip (LooksPanel.tsx:312): "The active layer gets the look's filters and effects, and atmosphere goes behind it. Grades and textures always cover the whole image." Document tooltip (:321): "Character filters go on the document's character. Image-wide filters (glitch, RGB split…) become adjustment layers over everything."
(b) Toast (engine.ts:659): when built.groupLayers is non-empty, say 'Applied look "X" (filters/effects on "Name"; grades and textures cover the whole image)' instead of 'to "Name"'.
(c) Optionally, if scoped looks are wanted, add an explicit third choice, "Only this layer". In insertLookDraft, insert the top group directly above the target in its parent list instead of at { parentId: null }, mark it clipped (or clip each child), and drop the behind layers. Do not make this the Layer default.

confirmed.title: Dropping a .psd (or .svg) onto a selected character offers 'Replace', which then fails with 'Could not read'
confirmed.issue: The canvas drop handler treats any file whose type starts with 'image/' as a render it can swap in. Chromium reports .psd as image/vnd.adobe.photoshop when the OS has that type registered (common on PCs with Photoshop installed); .svg and .tif also have image/ types. So with the template character selected, a dropped PSD gets the menu 'Replace Placeholder Character / Add as New Layer'. Choosing Replace tries to decode the PSD as a bitmap and fails with an error toast. Dropping the same PSD with no character selected opens it correctly as a document.
confirmed.evidence:
f13c-psd-replace.mjs: Crimson template (placeholder active), drop poster.psd of type image/vnd.adobe.photoshop on the canvas.
- The menu shows ['Replace Placeholder Character', 'Add as New Layer'].
- Replace shows the toast 'Could not read “poster.psd”' and logs 'console error: [replace] drop failed InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.' (shots/f13c-psd-replace.png).
f13b-psd-drop.mjs: the same PSD dropped on a blank document opens as a 23-layer document.

Code: src/roblox/character/index.tsx:123 `const isImageFile = (f: File) => f.type.startsWith('image/') || IMAGE_FILE_EXTS.some(...)`.
confirmed.fix: Only claim files the decoder can read. Decide by IMAGE_FILE_EXTS (png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif/bmp) plus an allow-list of raster MIME types, not the 'image/' prefix. Let .psd/.svg/.tif fall through to the normal open path, or offer 'Open as Document' for them.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch, and I did not fake the MIME type. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-e2e-flows-v5/v-psd-drop.mjs. The PSD is a 2-layer file I made with ag-psd (mkpsd.mjs → poster.psd). I loaded it through CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles, so Chromium picked File.type with its own lookup. It came back as 'image/vnd.adobe.photoshop', because this Linux box has shared-mime-info.

Results against snap-dist on :5396:
- **A. Crimson template, placeholder active, drop the PSD:** the overlay says "Drop one image to replace “Your Character (replace me)”". The menu is ['Replace Placeholder Character', 'Add as New Layer']. Choosing Replace shows the toast 'Could not read “poster.psd”' and logs '[replace] drop failed InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.' The document is unchanged.
- **B. Same drop, "Add as New Layer":** the PSD actually opens as a new 2-layer document. The label is wrong, but the result is usable.
- **D. Control, same PSD with an empty type (Windows with no .psd registration):** no menu appears and the PSD opens straight away as a document.

Cause:
- src/roblox/character/index.tsx:123 `isImageFile` accepts any `image/` MIME type.
- decodeImageFile (src/roblox/character/replace.ts:75) only calls createImageBitmap, which cannot decode a PSD.
- src/ui/shell/DropOverlay.tsx:74 asks the drop hook to claim the file before openFileWithIo. So the hook takes the file before the normal path, which would have opened the PSD as a document (dropMode treats psd as a project extension, docInfo.ts:104).

Which systems this hits:
- macOS: Chromium reports the same type for .psd everywhere (a dmg target exists in package.json).
- Linux: shown here.
- Windows (the main NSIS target): only when the registry gives .psd a Content Type. That is plausible on PCs with Photoshop installed, but not universal.

Severity minor is right. Nothing is lost, the error message is clear, and there are workarounds: "Add as New Layer", Shift-drop, selecting another layer, or File ▸ Open. The common trigger is dropping a PSD on a freshly created template, which leaves the placeholder selected.

One part of the finding is overstated. .svg and .tif fail on the normal path too: openFile's sniff() returns 'unknown' and throws, and DropOverlay shows the same 'Could not read' toast. For those types the hook only adds a pointless menu before the same failure. The real regression is PSD only.

The proposed fix is right, with two refinements:
1. In the claim, decide by extension using IMAGE_FILE_EXTS. Only fall back to MIME when there is no extension, and then only for a raster allow-list: image/png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp.
2. Explicitly refuse project files: psd/psb/pgfx extensions, or ctx.data starting with '8BPS'. The simplest way is to bail out early with `if (dropMode(ctx.file.name, ctx.hasDoc, ctx.shift) === 'new') return false;` together with an 8BPS magic check. Then PSDs always go to the normal open path.
verdict.betterFix:
In src/roblox/character/index.tsx, replace isImageFile with:

`const ext = (n) => n.toLowerCase().split('.').pop() ?? '';`

`const RASTER_MIME = /^image\/(png|jpeg|webp|gif|bmp)$/;`

`const isImageFile = (f, data) => { const e = ext(f.name); if (['psd','psb','pgfx'].includes(e)) return false; const b = new Uint8Array(data, 0, 4); if (b[0]===0x38&&b[1]===0x42&&b[2]===0x50&&b[3]===0x53) return false; return IMAGE_FILE_EXTS.includes(e) || (!f.name.includes('.') && RASTER_MIME.test(f.type)); }`

Then call `isImageFile(ctx.file, ctx.data)` in claim. Projects and PSDs fall through to openFileWithIo, which opens them as new documents. Optionally, make decodeImageFile's catch also try openFile as a fallback, so an undecodable file still opens instead of only showing an error toast.

confirmed.title: Save As writes the old (template) name into the .pgfx, so reopened projects show the template name, not the file name
confirmed.issue:
Save As encodes the document before the file dialog, while it still has its old name (e.g. 'Crimson Film Thumbnail'). Only after the file is written is the in-memory document renamed to the chosen file name, silently, and the tab is left clean. The user has no reason to save again, so the file on disk keeps the template name. On open, loadProject keeps the embedded name unless it is empty or 'Untitled', so the file name is ignored.

Result: every project made from a template, and every copy or renamed file, reopens with the same tab label and window title, and Export defaults to the template name. Users who save several thumbnails from one template can't tell their tabs apart, and every Export defaults to the same file name.
confirmed.evidence:
Script: names-drop.mjs (log: names-drop.log), run against the packaged asar.
- After Save As 'Poster.pgfx': session name 'Poster', title 'Poster — Perseverance', dirty false.
- Close, then File ▸ Open Poster.pgfx: name 'Crimson Film Thumbnail', title 'Crimson Film Thumbnail — Perseverance'.
- First "name" field inside Poster.pgfx: 'Crimson Film Thumbnail'.
- Export dialog default: 'Crimson Film Thumbnail.png'.

Production binary, prod-argv.log: double-click-style cold start of 'My Poster.pgfx' opens a tab named 'Crimson Film Thumbnail'.

dc1.log, 'Open Recent works after a relaunch': Poster.pgfx opens as 'Crimson Film Thumbnail'.

Expected: the tab, title and export default follow the file name, as in Photoshop.

- src/io/save.ts:62 `const data = await encodeProject(committed)` runs before the dialog.
- src/io/save.ts:91 `renameDocSilently(id, baseName(fileNameOf(result)))` runs after the write; the file is never rewritten.
- src/io/project.ts:197 `if (!doc.name || doc.name === 'Untitled') doc.name = baseName(file.name);`

1. In loadProject (src/io/project.ts:197), when `file.path` is set (desktop open, Explorer, Open Recent), always set `doc.name = baseName(file.name)`. The tab and title then follow the file, as in Photoshop.
2. In the Save As branch of saveDocument, make the file contain the new name: encode a copy of `committed` renamed to the chosen base name, then write it. For example, have desktop saveFile return the chosen path first and write with writeFile, or re-encode and write again after the dialog returns.

I reproduced this from scratch with my own script, not the reviewer's. - **B.** A second project from the same template, saved as 'Thumb 2.pgfx' and reopened: both tabs read 'Crimson Film Thumbnail'. Only the hover tooltip, which shows the path, tells them apart. The quit prompt for unsaved changes also lists documents by doc.name, so it would be just as ambiguous.

- src/io/save.ts:62 encodes the project before the dialog.
- src/io/save.ts:91 renames the document only in memory, after the write, and leaves the tab clean.
- src/io/project.ts:197 keeps the name stored in the file unless it is empty or 'Untitled'.

''); if (fromFile) doc.name = fromFile; else if (!doc.name) doc.name = 'Untitled';`. That covers File ▸ Open, Open Recent, Explorer/argv, drag-and-drop (path null) and the browser. confirmed.title: Dropping a .pgfx from Explorer onto the window opens a copy with no file path: Ctrl+S opens Save As, and dropping it again opens a duplicate
confirmed.issue:
The window's file-drop handler always passes `path: null` to openFileWithIo. The preload never exposes `webUtils.getPathForFile`, and File.path no longer exists in Electron 32 and later, so the renderer cannot know where a dropped file came from.

What the user gets from dragging a project onto the window:
- The project opens unlinked from its file.
- Ctrl+S opens Save As, defaulting to the template-derived name in the last folder, instead of saving the file they dropped. Users end up with their work in a different file while the original stays stale.
- The file is not added to Open Recent.
- focusOpenProject(null) cannot match an already-open copy, so dropping the same file again opens a second copy.

Dropped .psd and image files are also missing from Open Recent.
confirmed.evidence:
Script: names-drop.mjs part 2 (log: names-drop.log). The drop is synthetic (a JS File), but the handler passes `path: null` whatever Electron provides.
- After dropping Poster.pgfx: `{name:'Crimson Film Thumbnail', path:null}`.
- Edit, then Ctrl+S: Save As dialog shown with defaultPath ['Crimson Film Thumbnail.pgfx']; 'original file modified: false'.
- Dropping the same file again: two sessions, both with path null.
- Recent files unchanged.

Code:
- src/ui/shell/DropOverlay.tsx:75 `openFileWithIo({ path: null, name: f.name, data }, ...)`.
- electron/preload.cjs requires only contextBridge, ipcRenderer and webFrame; there is no webUtils.
- webutils-probe/ (stock Electron 44, sandboxed preload) prints `PROBE {"hasWebUtils":true,"fn":"function"}`, so the API is available to the preload.
confirmed.fix:
In preload, expose one function, e.g. `desktop.openDroppedFile(file)`. It calls `webUtils.getPathForFile(file)` in the isolated world, so the page cannot forge paths: a JS-constructed File returns ''. If a path comes back, it invokes a new main-process handler that grants that path (same checks as dialog grants: isSafeAbsPath, not a FIFO or device, openable extension) and returns the path.

DropOverlay then calls openFileWithIo with `{ path, name, data }`. That gets loadProject linking the session to its file, addRecentFile, and focusOpenProject deduplication for free. Fall back to `path: null` only when no path is available (browser build).

verdict.note:
I reproduced this in the real Electron 44.5.1 app using the snapshot's own build. I used a native file drop (CDP Input.dispatchDragEvent with `files`, which creates real disk-backed File objects like an Explorer drop), not a File built in JS. The app ran from a scratch app root, rv-packaged-app-v1/app, which holds copies of electron/*.cjs, package.json and snap-dist. Script: rv-packaged-app-v1/drop-path.mjs, log: drop-path.log.

Observed:
- The renderer sees the drop with no path: no `File.path` (removed in Electron 32+), and the bridge has no path API.
- After dropping Poster.pgfx, the session is `{name:'Crimson Film Thumbnail', path:null}` and Open Recent stays `[]`.
- Edit, then Ctrl+S: the Save As dialog appears with defaultPath `['Crimson Film Thumbnail.pgfx']`, a bare file name, so the dialog opens in the OS's last-used folder, not the dropped file's folder. The original file is not modified.
- Dropping the same file again gives 2 sessions, both with path null.
- Control test: File > Open of the same file links the session (path set, added to Recent). Dropping the file while that linked copy is open still adds a second, unlinked copy, so focusOpenProject deduplication is skipped for drops.

Cause:
- src/ui/shell/DropOverlay.tsx:75 always passes `path: null`.
- electron/preload.cjs:2 never imports webUtils.
- Downstream:
  - src/io/project.ts:198 opens with filePath null.
  - src/io/open.ts:70/72/84 call focusOpenProject(null), which returns false, and addRecentFile(null), which does nothing.
  - src/io/save.ts:63/84 falls through to Save As with the name stored inside the document.

HANDOFF.md:111-113 lists Explorer double-click, File > Open and Open Recent as linked and deduplicated, but not drag-drop. This is not a known gap.

Why major is right and blocker is not: nothing is overwritten silently, because Save As always appears. But drag-to-open is a common Windows workflow. A user who clicks Save in that dialog ends up with their work in a differently named file in another folder, while the file they dropped stays stale. Next time they open it, their edits appear lost. Dropped PSDs also never reach Open Recent (minor).

Testing the fix: a copy of the preload, rv-packaged-app-v1/app-fixed (script drop-path-fixed.mjs, log drop-path-fixed.log), adds `webUtils` to the require and exposes `pathForFile: f => webUtils.getPathForFile(f)`. In the sandboxed, context-isolated preload, the native drop returns the real absolute path. A JS-built `new File(['x'], '/etc/passwd.pgfx')` returns ''. So the reviewer's approach works and the page cannot forge a path.

confirmed.title: The installed app uses about 24% of a CPU core forever while idle: loading-placeholder animations on off-screen asset cards in the default Libraries panel never stop
confirmed.issue:
Every asset card that has not been scrolled into view keeps an infinite CSS loading animation (a shimmer on `.assets-skel`). Thumbnails are only requested when a card intersects the viewport, so the 51 cards below the fold in the default Essentials Libraries panel animate for as long as the app is open: on the start screen, with documents open, at any time.

This is a non-composited background-position animation, so the renderer and GPU process produce frames continuously even though no JS is running. Laptop users will see fans spinning and battery draining with the app just sitting open.

The numbers below were measured on software GL (xvfb/SwiftShader). That is also what VMs and blocklisted GPUs use, which the app explicitly supports via enable-unsafe-swiftshader. Hardware GPUs make each frame cheaper but still produce frames continuously.
confirmed.evidence:
idle-skel.mjs, production binary, fresh profile, 12 s after boot:
- 51 `.assets-skel` elements in the assets-panel, 0 of them in the viewport.
- Renderer + GPU process CPU with the animations running: 23.6% of a core.
- After injecting `.assets-skel{animation:none!important}`: 0.0%.

idle-anim.mjs: 51 running 'assets-shimmer' animations on the start screen and the same 51 with a template open. Over 3 s idle: RecalcStyleCount 180, TaskDuration 0.51 s.

idle-raf.mjs: 0 requestAnimationFrame calls per second; the CPU profile is 88% idle in JS.

Screenshot: idle-skel.png (Libraries panel with assets below the fold).

Code:
- src/assets/ui/AssetThumb.tsx:69 `{!ready && <div className="assets-skel" />}`; the thumbnail is only requested from the IntersectionObserver at lines 49-57.
- src/assets/assets.css:194-200 `animation: assets-shimmer 1.4s linear infinite`.
confirmed.fix:
Animate the placeholder only while a thumbnail is actually being produced for a visible card. Options:
- Keep a `near` state set by the IntersectionObserver callback (which already exists) and add the shimmer class only when `near && !ready`; off-screen cards get a static placeholder.
- Or default to `.assets-skel{animation-play-state:paused}` and run it under `.assets-thumb.near`.
- Or add `content-visibility:auto` to the asset cards and the scroll list.

Also add a check, for example in electron-desktop-check, that `document.getAnimations()` is empty on an idle start screen.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch in the real Electron app, using the snapshot's production dist and a fresh profile (XDG_CONFIG_HOME isolated). Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-packaged-app-v2/: idle-verify.mjs and idle-verify2.mjs, plus the screenshot idle-start.png.

What I saw, 12 s after boot on the start screen:
- The Libraries/Assets panel is open by default in the Essentials layout and shows 59 assets.
- 51 `.assets-skel` elements exist and none of them are visible.
- `document.getAnimations()` returns 51 running 'assets-shimmer' animations and nothing else.

CPU over 8–10 s windows, measured from /proc for the whole Electron process tree:

| State | App CPU | Main thread busy (CDP TaskDuration) | Style recalcs/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start screen | 18.5–18.8% | 11.5% | 60 |
| Template open | 23.8% | 16.1% | 60 |
| Window hidden with `w.hide()` | 23.5% | 16.1% | 60 |
| Start screen, `.assets-skel{animation:none}` | 1.4% | – | – |

- The hidden case still shows `visibilityState` 'visible', because electron/main.cjs:457 sets `backgroundThrottling:false`. A minimised window could not be tested: there is no window manager under xvfb.
- The skeletons never go away by themselves. They were still there after more than 60 s.
- They come back on every launch. src/assets/lib/thumbs.ts saves only render costs to localStorage, not the thumbnails themselves.

Root cause, as the reviewer described it:
- src/assets/ui/AssetThumb.tsx:69 renders the skeleton whenever `!ready`.
- The thumbnail is only requested when the IntersectionObserver fires (lines 49-57, `rootMargin: 160px`).
- src/assets/assets.css:194-200 runs an infinite background-position animation on that skeleton. Background-position is not composited, so it is main-thread style and paint work 60 times a second.
- One running skeleton is enough to keep the 60 Hz lifecycle going, so the fix has to bring the idle count to zero.
- I found no handling for this anywhere else. It is not in HANDOFF.md's known gaps or in the excluded list.

Corrections to the report:
1. Almost all the cost is in the renderer. The GPU process measured about 0.7%, so the "renderer + GPU produce frames" framing overstates the GPU side. The main-thread busy time (11–18%) does not depend on the GPU, so a hardware GPU will not remove most of it. That keeps it at major: every user pays a constant idle CPU and battery cost whenever the app is open.
2. Fix option 3 (`content-visibility:auto` on the cards) does not work in this Chromium. I injected `.assets-card{content-visibility:auto;contain-intrinsic-size:auto 120px}` and still saw 51 running animations, 60 recalcs/s and 27% CPU.
3. Option 2 works. Injecting `.assets-skel{animation-play-state:paused}` gave 0 running animations, 0 recalcs/s and 1.9% CPU.
verdict.betterFix:
Gate the shimmer on "requested and not ready", not on "not ready". The only file to change is src/assets/ui/AssetThumb.tsx, and the change covers AssetGrid (the panel and the Libraries dialog) and MyAssetsTab.

1. Add `const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)`.
2. Call `setLoading(false)` when the effect resets, at the same point as `setReady(false)`.
3. In the IntersectionObserver callback, call `setLoading(true)` right before `cancel = requestThumb(...)`.
4. Render the placeholder as `{!ready && <div className={`assets-skel${loading ? ' loading' : ''}`} />}`.
5. In src/assets/assets.css, move the animation off `.assets-skel` and onto `.assets-skel.loading`. `.assets-skel` keeps its static background, so off-screen cards show a flat placeholder.

Failure is already covered: thumbs.ts draws a red fallback when a render fails and still calls `draw`, so `ready` always ends up true and no shimmer runs forever.

Simplest alternative: drop the animation and keep a static placeholder, since thumbnails render in tens of milliseconds.

Do not rely on `content-visibility:auto`; I measured that it does not stop the animations.

Add a regression check, for example in scripts/electron-desktop-check.mjs: after about 10 s on the idle start screen, `document.getAnimations().filter(a => a.playState === 'running').length === 0`.

confirmed.title: Blank window, with no error shown, when the app is installed in a folder whose path contains '%'
confirmed.issue:
`w.loadFile(INDEX_HTML)` builds the page URL with url.format, which leaves '%' unescaped. Chromium keeps it too, giving URLs like `.../100%%20Art/...`. The file:// request filter, lib.fileUrlInside, calls fileURLToPath, which throws URIError on that malformed escape and returns false. onBeforeRequest therefore cancels the app's own index.html, and the window shows chrome-error://chromewebdata/.

A folder name containing a valid escape such as 'x%41y' fails the same way, because it decodes to a different path. isAppUrl (main.cjs:96) has the same flaw, so IPC is refused as well.

Triggers:
- Windows user names may contain '%'. The profile folder is the default per-user install root (C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local\Programs\Perseverance), and the portable exe extracts under %TEMP%, inside the same profile.
- The NSIS installer lets users pick any install folder, e.g. 'D:\100% Tools'.

Affected users get an app that never starts.
confirmed.evidence:
install-paths.mjs runs the production binary from hard-linked copies of linux-unpacked (logs: install-paths.log, install-paths3.log).
- FAIL: '100% Art', 'Ünïcödé 100%', 'x%41y'. Page href is `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`. main.log: `[warn] blocked file request file:///.../100%%20Art/Perseverance/resources/app.asar/dist/index.html` and `[error] did-fail-load -20 ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`.
- OK: 'José', 'Пользователь', '用户', "O'Brien", 'A & B', 'Tom (Work)', 'a#b', 'C++ stuff', 'semi;colon', 'braces{1}' (under a UTF-8 locale).

run-fix.mjs, extracted app run from '100% Fix/':
- Original: ui false; IPC refused with 'ENOTGRANTED: desktop:user-data from an untrusted frame'.
- With main.cjs:540 changed to `w.loadURL(require('node:url').pathToFileURL(INDEX_HTML).href)`: ui true, href `.../100%25%20Fix/app/dist/index.html`, IPC ok, no warnings.

Code:
- electron/main.cjs:540 `else w.loadFile(INDEX_HTML);`
- electron/main.cjs:794-798, the onBeforeRequest filter.
- electron/lib.cjs:67-78 fileUrlInside.
- electron/main.cjs:90-99 isAppUrl.
confirmed.fix:
Load the page with `w.loadURL(pathToFileURL(INDEX_HTML).href)` instead of loadFile. pathToFileURL escapes '%', '#' and '?', so every request URL round-trips through fileURLToPath, and both fileUrlInside and isAppUrl work unchanged.

Add a desktop-check case that launches from a temp folder named like '100% x#y' and asserts the UI comes up.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch in two setups, both under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-packaged-app-v3/.

1) Unpackaged Electron running the snapshot's electron/ code and dist build from install folders with test names.
- Script: pct-path.mjs; log: pct-path.log.
- 'plain' and 'a#b ?q': the UI loads and IPC works.
- '100% Art' and 'x%41y': the page never loads (no UI) and IPC fails with "ENOTGRANTED: desktop:user-data from an untrusted frame".
- main.log shows `blocked file request file:///.../inst/100%%20Art/app/dist/index.html`, then `did-fail-load -20 ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`.
- Closing the window also hangs for 4 s ("close request not acknowledged by the renderer") because the close-ack is refused.

2) The real packaged binary (asar plus fuses), from hard-linked copies of rv-packaged-app/pkg/linux-unpacked.
- I checked first that its app.asar main.cjs and lib.cjs are byte-identical to the snapshot.
- Script: pct-pkg2.mjs, which connects over CDP because the inspect fuse blocks Playwright's _electron launcher. Log: pct-pkg.log.
- 'plainpkg': ui true.
- '100% Art': href is chrome-error://chromewebdata/, ui false, IPC refused, same blocked/did-fail-load lines. The user gets a blank window with no dialog.

Root cause is as the reviewer describes:
- electron/main.cjs:540 calls `w.loadFile(INDEX_HTML)`. Electron builds that URL with url.format, which escapes only '#' and '?', so a literal '%' stays.
- electron/lib.cjs:67-78 `fileUrlInside`: fileURLToPath throws URIError on '%%20' and the function returns false, so the onBeforeRequest filter (electron/main.cjs:794-797) cancels index.html.
- electron/main.cjs:87-99 `isAppUrl` fails the same way, so every IPC call is refused.
- With 'x%41y', even Chromium decodes the URL to 'xAy'. Plain loadFile therefore cannot work there whatever the filter does.

Not a known gap: HANDOFF.md:95-107 lists the app:// scheme only as a "possible later step" and says nothing about '%' paths. The webRequest filter added in Desktop R2 made this worse: before it, the page loaded but IPC was already broken.

Fix verified: in a scratch copy ('100% Fix'), changing main.cjs:540 to `else w.loadURL(require('node:url').pathToFileURL(INDEX_HTML).href);` gives ui true, href `.../100%25%20Fix/app/dist/index.html`, IPC ok and no warnings.
- Reloads (main.cjs:342, 366) use webContents.reload(), so they keep the corrected URL.
- For ordinary paths, pathToFileURL produces the same URL that loadFile+Chromium did (UTF-8 percent-encoding, %23/%3F). The file:// localStorage origin is unchanged, so no migration is needed.

Severity: I'd lower it from major to minor.
- Impact is total for affected users: the app never starts and shows no error.
- But the trigger is rare: a '%' in the Windows profile name (which also covers the portable exe's %TEMP% extraction) or a hand-picked install folder containing '%'.
- It is not a "common workflow", so major overstates it. It is still a cheap, low-risk one-line fix that should go in before release.

Extra fix suggestions are in betterFix.
verdict.betterFix:
The reviewer's fix is right: in electron/main.cjs:540, replace `w.loadFile(INDEX_HTML)` with `w.loadURL(pathToFileURL(INDEX_HTML).href)`, taking `pathToFileURL` from 'node:url'. Leave fileUrlInside and isAppUrl unchanged; making them "tolerant" is the wrong fix, because Chromium itself decodes valid escapes like '%41'.

Two additions:
(a) In the did-fail-load handler (main.cjs:522-525), when a main-frame load fails in production with a code other than -3, show dialog.showErrorBox with the error and the main.log path, so the user doesn't just get a blank window.
(b) Add tests:
- a desktopMain.test.ts unit case asserting that `lib.fileUrlInside(pathToFileURL(path.join(dist, 'index.html')).href, dist)` is true for dist roots containing '%', '%41', '#', '?' and spaces, on both linux and win32;
- an electron-desktop-check case that launches from a temp folder named like '100% x#y' and asserts the UI comes up and IPC is trusted.

confirmed.title: Native "Quit Anyway" says autosave may recover unsaved work, but the autosave copies are deleted on the next launch
confirmed.issue:
The main process's fallback prompts tell the user that quitting loses unsaved changes but that 'autosave may offer to recover them on the next launch'. These are: renderer not acknowledging the close, renderer prompt stuck, and closeUnguarded.

closeNow() then closes the window normally. The page's pagehide handler, markClosedWithoutSaving, records every dirty autosaved document as deliberately closed without saving, and offerRecovery discards those entries on the next start.

A user who force-quits a busy or stuck window, trusting the message, loses the work. Only a hard crash or kill keeps recovery. The comment on the session-end handler ('autosave keeps unsaved work for recovery') fails the same way whenever the window closes normally after session-end, which is how the repo's own desktop check models it.
confirmed.evidence:
recovery.mjs (log: recovery.log), packaged asar:
- A: SIGKILL after an autosave. Relaunch offers 'Recover unsaved documents?' and the document is restored (marker guide present).
- C: dirty document autosaved. Close shows the in-app prompt; closing again after 3 s shows the native 'Quit without answering the editor?', whose detail includes 'autosave may offer to recover them on the next launch'. Choosing Quit Anyway exits with code 0. On relaunch: 'recovery offered = false', 0 dialogs.
- B: the check's session-end then close sequence also gives 'recovery offered = false'.

Code:
- electron/main.cjs:290 and 319 contain the prompt texts.
- electron/main.cjs:223-229, closeNow calls w.close().
- src/io/autosave.ts:212-221 markClosedWithoutSaving, registered on pagehide at :256.
- src/io/autosave.ts:232 discards the marked entries.
confirmed.fix:
Only the renderer's own "Don't Save" answer should mark documents as discarded.

Before any force close it initiates (closeFallback / closeUnguarded 'Quit Anyway', unresponsive 'Quit', session-end, crash prompt 'Quit'), main sends a `desktop:keep-recovery` message, which preload delivers synchronously, or sets a flag the preload exposes. markClosedWithoutSaving does nothing when that flag is set.

Alternatively, have the close-confirm path write the closedDirty marker explicitly when the user picks "Don't Save", rather than doing it on every pagehide.

verdict.note:
Reproduced. I wrote my own script and ran it in real Electron against the snapshot's production build. The app was a scratch copy of electron/ plus snap-dist, with an isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME, autosaveMinutes=0.01, and native dialogs stubbed in main.

Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-packaged-app-v4/recovery-verify.mjs
Logs: recovery-verify.log and recovery-uicrash.log in the same folder.

Every scenario starts the same way: open a template, add a marker guide, and wait until autosave has written the IndexedDB entry. Then the app is relaunched and checked.

- **kill (control):** SIGKILL. Recovery is offered and the marker guide comes back.
- **stuck:** close, the in-app 'Save changes before closing?' appears, close again after 1.8 s (REPEAT_CLOSE_MS=1500). The native box 'Quit without answering the editor?' appears, whose detail ends '...autosave may offer to recover them on the next launch'. Choosing Quit Anyway exits with code 0. On relaunch recovery is not offered and IndexedDB has 0 entries: the entry was deleted.
- **uiCrash (new, worse than the reported cases):** a dialog throws while rendering. DialogHost (src/App.tsx:89) is not inside any ErrorBoundary, so React unmounts the whole root and the window goes blank (no .shell-root, empty body). Shell's useEffect cleanup (src/ui/shell/Shell.tsx:44) removes the close listener while the dirty sessions and the pagehide listener stay. Closing the window shows the closeUnguarded box 'Quit Perseverance? ... autosave may offer to recover them on the next launch'. The user's only choices are Cancel (stay in a blank window that cannot save) or Quit Anyway. Quit Anyway exits 0, and on relaunch there is no recovery and 0 entries. This is the situation recovery exists for, and the app deletes the only copy right after promising it.
- **sessionEnd (the repo check's model: emit session-end, then close()):** no recovery, 0 entries. On real Windows the process is most likely just terminated after WM_ENDSESSION, so pagehide would not run. I could not verify that on Linux, so treat this part as unproven.
- **discard (reference):** the in-app Discard answer also drops recovery, which is intended.

Part of the finding is not reproduced. In the busy/no-ack path, I blocked the renderer with a 4 s synchronous loop, the native box said 'Perseverance is not responding' and I chose Quit Anyway. Recovery was still offered and restored: the busy renderer never ran pagehide. The crash prompt 'Quit' cannot be affected either, because the renderer is already dead.

Root cause: src/io/autosave.ts:205-220 assumes that any normal unload means 'the user quit and chose not to save'. Line 256 registers markClosedWithoutSaving on every pagehide, and offerRecovery deletes the marked entries at line 232. But closeNow() (electron/main.cjs:223-229, w.close()) is also reached from main's own force paths: closeFallback at :305, closeUnguarded at :324, and unresponsive 'Quit' at :407. When the renderer is still responsive, those paths unload the page normally. The prompt texts at main.cjs:290 and :319 promise the opposite. The file:line pointers in the finding are accurate, and HANDOFF.md does not list this as a known gap.

Severity: I raise it from minor to major. The stuck path alone is minor-ish because the user had a working Save button. In the UI-crash path the user has no way to save, the native prompt promises recovery, and choosing Quit Anyway silently destroys the autosave entry, so unsaved work since the last save is lost for certain.
verdict.betterFix:
Use the reviewer's alternative, not the IPC flag. A main→renderer 'desktop:keep-recovery' message sent just before w.close() races the page unload. It also has to be repeated on every current and future force-close path.

Make the discard marker explicit instead:

1. In src/io/autosave.ts, export markClosedWithoutSaving (for example as `markDiscardedOnQuit()`). In the desktop build, drop `window.addEventListener('pagehide', markClosedWithoutSaving)` at :256. If you want to keep the browser build's current behaviour, keep it only for that build: `if (!desktop) addEventListener('pagehide', ...)`.
2. In src/ui/shell/desktopIntegration.ts confirmQuit, change the discard branch to `if (choice === 'discard') { markDiscardedOnQuit(); return true; }`. It runs synchronously, before desktop.confirmClose(true). The Save path needs nothing, because saved sessions turn clean and the store subscriber already removes their entries.

After this change, every exit the user did not answer with the in-app Discard keeps the recovery entries, so the existing prompt texts become true. That covers closeFallback 'stuck', closeUnguarded after a UI crash, unresponsive Quit, session-end, the forced destroy and kills.

Separately, wrap DialogHost and MenuHost (src/App.tsx:89-90) in an ErrorBoundary, as a defence in depth, so a single broken dialog cannot blank the whole window and remove the close guard.

Add a regression check to scripts/electron-desktop-check.mjs. Make a document dirty, force autosave, take the stuck → Quit Anyway path, relaunch, and assert that 'Recover unsaved documents?' is shown. Add a matching assertion that the in-app Discard path is not offered recovery.

confirmed.title: electron-builder exits with code 1 after building the installers when it can't detect a GitHub repo (source zip, git worktree)
confirmed.issue:
package.json has no `repository` field and no `build.publish` setting. When electron-builder can't read a GitHub remote from .git/config, it gets a null publish config and crashes in updateInfoBuilder.computeChannelNames. This happens after the NSIS, portable and AppImage files are already written, so `npm run dist:win` / `dist:linux` exit with code 1.

This hits anyone following README 'Build from source' from a 'Download ZIP' copy or a git worktree. They see a failed build even though the installers exist, and anything chained after the command doesn't run. CI is unaffected because actions/checkout provides the origin remote. The app has no auto-updater, so update-info generation, and the shipped resources/app-update.yml, are unused anyway.
confirmed.evidence:
- eb-win.log: Windows NSIS and portable built (Perseverance-Setup-0.1.0.exe 142.7 MB, Perseverance-Portable-0.1.0.exe 142.5 MB in win/), then '⨯ Cannot read properties of null (reading \'channel\') at computeChannelNames (app-builder-lib/src/publish/updateInfoBuilder.ts:47)', EXIT 1.
- eb-appimage.log: the same after Perseverance-0.1.0.AppImage was built; that AppImage boots fine (appimage-boot.mjs).
- Both logs say 'Cannot detect repository by .git/config'; the snapshot's .git is a worktree file.
- eb-appimage-fix.log: the same build in a scratch copy with `build.publish = null` exits 0.
confirmed.fix: Add `"publish": null` to the `build` section of package.json, since there is no updater (this also stops generating update metadata). Or add `"repository": "github:noxiryn/perseverance"`. Either one lets local builds without a detectable remote finish with exit code 0.

verdict.note:
The bug is real and minor, but it hits far fewer people than the finding says. A missing GitHub remote alone does not cause it. The build only fails when a GitHub token is also set in the environment (GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, or GITLAB_TOKEN, KEYGEN_TOKEN or BITBUCKET_TOKEN). This sandbox has GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN set, which is why the reviewer, and an earlier run in scratchpad/rel-build.log, saw it.

**Why the token matters** (node_modules/app-builder-lib/out/publish/PublishManager.js):
- With no `build.publish` set, `resolvePublishConfigurations` (around line 362) only picks a publish provider when a token variable is set. If GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN is set it picks `github`.
- It then calls `getResolvedPublishConfig`. When no repo can be found, `getInfo()` (around line 463) logs "Cannot detect repository by .git/config" and returns null.
- That gives a publish config list of `[null]`, and `computeChannelNames` in updateInfoBuilder.js reads `publishConfig.channel` on null and crashes.
- With no token, the list is `[]`. `getPublishConfigsForUpdateInfo` finds no repo, no update-info tasks are created, and the build exits 0. The "Cannot detect repository" warning itself only ever appears on the token path.

**Builds I ran** (scratch: rv-packaged-app-v5/; `proj/` is a copy of the snapshot's package.json, electron/, build/ and snap-dist with no .git):

| Run | Log | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Linux AppImage, token set | eb-appimage-token.log | AppImage written, then "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'channel')", exit 1 |
| Linux AppImage, `env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN` | eb-appimage-notoken.log | exit 0, no warning, no app-update.yml |
| Windows NSIS + portable, no token | eb-win-notoken.log | both .exe files built, exit 0 |
| Fake worktree (`.git` is a file), no token | eb-appimage-wt-notoken.log | exit 0; the ENOTDIR error is already handled by `orNullIfFileNotExist` |
| Token set, `build.publish: null` (fix-null/) | eb-appimage-fix-null.log | exit 0, no update metadata |
| Token set, `repository: "github:noxiryn/perseverance"` (fix-repo/) | eb-appimage-fix-repo.log | exit 0, but writes latest-linux.yml and app-update.yml |

**Corrections to the finding:**
- It does not hit "anyone following README Build from source from a Download ZIP or worktree". Someone without a token exported gets exit 0 on both `dist:win` and `dist:linux`.
- It does hit developers who build from a ZIP copy or a git worktree while a token is exported. That includes people who export GH_TOKEN for the gh CLI, worktrees inside Codespaces, and agent containers like this one. A normal clone with a GitHub origin is fine.
- The installers are complete in every case. Only the exit code and anything chained after the command are affected.
- End users installing the release are never affected.
- CI is unaffected: it does not export a token into the build steps, it passes `--publish never`, and the checkout provides an origin remote.

Minor is the right severity, at low priority.

**Fix:** the proposed fix is right. The better option is adding `"publish": null` to the `build` section of package.json (it would sit at about line 216, before the closing brace of `build`). There is no electron-updater, so the update metadata is dead weight, and this also stops the unused app-update.yml going into CI-built apps. Adding `repository` also works, but it keeps generating update files nothing uses. It is still fine to add it for npm metadata.
verdict.betterFix: Add `"publish": null` under `build` in package.json. Builds then exit 0 whatever the environment (token set or not, git remote or not), and the unused latest*.yml and app-update.yml files are no longer generated. Optionally also add `"repository": "github:noxiryn/perseverance"` for npm metadata, but on its own it keeps producing unused update files. The finding's description should also change: the trigger is "a GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN-style variable is exported AND no GitHub origin can be detected", not "no GitHub remote".

confirmed.title: Create/Release Clipping Mask onto a pass-through group leaves a stale canvas and a stale File ▸ Export
confirmed.issue:
When a layer is clipped onto or released from a pass-through group, or a pass-through group itself becomes clipped, the incremental composite keeps the old pixels over the whole group area. The full compositor changes how the group composites: it is rendered isolated as a clip base instead of its children being inlined. But docItems() expands inline pass-through groups into marker items with layer:null, so itemRegion() returns null for them and planIncremental() computes no dirty area for the group. Only the toggled layer's own rectangle is recomposited.

The viewport and File ▸ Export (renderForExport → renderDocument, which starts incrementally from the viewport's cached full composite) show the old blend. Reopening the project or any later full composite shows a different image. The visible difference appears whenever the group contains non-Normal blend layers (Multiply/Screen/Overlay shading and lighting, very common in character groups) or adjustment layers. With an adjustment inside the group, the stale area extends over the whole canvas. Undo/redo of the toggle is stale too. The same result occurs at 064b27f, so this predates the diff.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro script: rv-render-paint-diff/clipgroup.full.js (`node run.mjs --script clipgroup.full.js`).

Steps:
- Create a 400×300 document with a Photo layer.
- Add Group 1 (pass-through) containing a 300×200 layer set to Multiply.
- Add a Texture layer above the group, select it, and run the real command runCommand('layer.clip') (Alt+Ctrl+G).

Observed: EXP.renderForExport(doc, {png, scale 1}) differs from a from-scratch render over the whole group area: box [20,40,300,200], 160,800 px, max 212 levels. Sample pixel: export [60,21,43] (still multiplied) vs fresh [255,48,48]. The viewport canvas differs from a forced full redraw by 212 over 988,866 device px.

Expected: identical.

The fuzzer (fuzz2.js, seed 5) minimises this to a single step, 'prop G.clipped=true': shared render off by up to 213 over 107,878 px. The 064b27f build gives identical numbers.

Code: src/render/engine.ts:2236-2241 (docItems inlines the group with marker items whose layer is null), :2246 (itemRegion(null) returns null), :2306-2343 (planIncremental unions only the changed items' regions), :2154 (compositeList composites the group isolated through renderLayer/compositeClipStack as soon as clipped layers follow it or it is clipped).
confirmed.fix: Never inline a pass-through group whose compositing depends on its neighbours. In docItems (engine.ts:2236) use `if (l.type === 'group' && isShown(rc, l) && inlinePassThrough(l) && !l.clipped && !rc.doc.layers[ids[i + 1]]?.clipped)` and otherwise push the group as a normal item (sig = listSig, layer = l). A clip toggle then changes the raw item list and planIncremental returns null (full composite). Add a regression test: toggle `clipped` on a layer above a pass-through group that has a Multiply child, then compare renderDocument with a render after invalidateRenderCache().

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch on the stock production build (snap-dist, port 5393), using only window.__app, the real commands and shortcut (layer.clip / layer.releaseClip / Alt+Ctrl+G), and real File > Quick Export PNG downloads. Each result is compared with the same document reopened under a new id, which forces a full composite.

The code argument holds. docItems (engine.ts:2236) always inlines a pass-through group as marker items with layer:null, so itemRegion returns null (:2246). planIncremental (:2306) then dirties only the toggled layer's own rect, and when the group itself is clipped it dirties nothing. But compositeList (:2154) switches the group to an isolated clip base as soon as a shown clipped layer follows it or it is clipped. The viewport stores the scale-1 slot, so renderForExport → renderDocument also goes incremental and comes out stale.

**Synthetic results** (script: rv-render-paint-diff-v0/clipgroup-ui.mjs). Setup: 400x300 document; pass-through group holding Body plus a Multiply child that hangs past Body; an 80x80 Texture layer above the group.
- **Create Clipping Mask:** export differs from the fresh render by 2800 px, max 167, box [100,240,140,20]. The viewport differs by 17350 device px.
- **Same stale result** for clipping the group itself (Alt+Ctrl+G on the group), Release Clipping Mask from a clean clipped state, and Redo.
- **Adjustment (invert) inside the group:** 100% of the canvas differs, max 255.
- **Normal-blend children only:** 0 diff, as expected.

**Realistic results** (script: looks-ui.mjs, 1280x720 photo, Gothic Paper look applied from the Looks panel):
- Selecting the "Look:" group and pressing Alt+Ctrl+G: the canvas and export still show the look over the whole image, while the fresh render differs on 100% of pixels (max 245). See out/look-gothic-paper-clipLookGroup-export-after.png vs -export-fresh.png.
- Adding a 300x200 "VS" layer above the look group and clipping it: 77.7% of pixels differ.
- The image later jumps to the true render on reopen or after any structural edit.

**Limits on when it triggers:**
- A clipped layer covering more than about 55% (export) / 70% (viewport) of the canvas forces a full composite and is correct. So the common doc-sized "New Layer, then Alt+Ctrl+G" flow is not affected.
- The Crimson template's Smoke and Film groups show no difference, because their backdrop is near-black.
- Clipping a group itself is stale at any size, since the group marker contributes no dirty region.

**Severity:** major is right. No crash or data loss (the saved document is correct), but the canvas and export disagree with the true render of the saved file.

**Proposed fix is incomplete.** I applied it to a scratch copy (fixA) and rebuilt. It fixes create, release and clip-group, including the adjustment and Looks cases. But toggling the eye of a clipped layer above a pass-through group is still stale: 2800 px, or 100% with the adjustment. compositeList only counts *shown* clipped layers, so hiding the only clipped layer switches the group back to inline. The `ids[i+1]?.clipped` check ignores visibility, so the item list does not change and only the hidden layer's rect is redrawn. The same eye-toggle bug exists in the current code.

The better fix (fixB) is in betterFix. With it, every case above (synthetic, eye toggle, undo/redo and both Looks cases) gives 0 diff. Render and panels vitest (119 tests) pass and tsc is clean.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-render-paint-diff-v0/: clipgroup-ui.mjs, looks-ui.mjs, tpl-ui.mjs, out/*.png, fixA/ and fixB/ (patched copies), dist-fixA/ and dist-fixB/.

confirmed.title: Changing Stroke/Bevel size on semi-transparent layers keeps the wrong width (cached distance fields of another depth are reused)
confirmed.issue:
LayerFields.distance() reuses any inherited field whose maxDist is at least the requested depth. When a size is being dragged up it also computes 'headroom' fields deeper than fieldBucket(maxDist). But edgeDistance() bounds partially covered (soft) pixels by their own coverage whenever an edge lies within depth + 2, so the values of soft pixels depend on the field depth. Distances are not 'exact below maxDist' for semi-transparent content.

Result: on soft content an inside or center Stroke (or Bevel) stays as wide as the largest size set earlier in the session. Soft content includes soft-brush paint below 100% opacity, smoke and glow assets, feathered cut-outs, and layers with a blur smart filter. The wrong render is cached and used for the canvas, thumbnails and exports until something invalidates it. The same result occurs at 064b27f.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro scripts: rv-render-paint-diff/fieldsoft.full.js (drag down) and fieldsoft-up.full.js (drag up).

Setup: a 600×400 layer with a 70%-opacity red block and an 85%-opacity blue disc. Add a Stroke at size 14, then drag the size slider to 2 the way the Effects panel does it (preview() on each step, then commit).

Observed, renderForExport-equivalent renderDocument vs a from-scratch render:

I reproduced this from scratch with my own scripts, on an instrumented build of the snapshot in my scratch dir, served on port 5394. The finding is real. The root cause is one level deeper than the report says: on semi-transparent content even a from-scratch render draws the wrong width.

Setup for every run: a 600x400 raster layer with a 70%-alpha red block.

**Inside Stroke widths, measured along a row of the block** (script rv-render-paint-diff-v1/soft.js)
- Opaque control: 2→2 px and 14→14 px. Cached and fresh renders are identical (0 px diff) for inside, center and outside, both when lowering 14→2 and when dragging 2→14.

- 70%-alpha, slider drag 2→14 with preview, then commit: 29 px from the headroom field, vs 21 px fresh. That is 17,280 px off.
- Center stroke is also wrong (17,724 px off). Outside is exact.

**Real export path** (rv-render-paint-diff-v1/export.js)
- `renderForExport` at 1x PNG, after editing the stroke 14→2, outputs a 21 px band. From scratch it outputs 7 px.
- Images: export-afterEdit.png and export-fromScratch.png. The intended width is 2 px.
- Export does not drop render caches, so what gets exported depends on the edit history.
- This breaks the HANDOFF claim that "renderDocument / thumbnails / exports are exact at all times".
- It is not a listed known gap. It is not handled anywhere else: the engine.ts:706 reuse check has no softness test.

**Why it happens**
- distance.ts:269-273, in `envelope()`: every pixel with coverage strictly between 0 and 255 is capped at its own-coverage bound `a/255-0.5`. That is about 0.2 px at 70% alpha.
- The cap applies whenever an edge site is within maxDist+2. Pixels farther out are clamped to maxDist.
- For uniformly semi-transparent content, every pixel within B+2 of the edge (B = field depth) therefore gets distance about 0.2. An inside or center stroke then covers a band of about B+2 px, not `size` px.
- Fresh render: B = fieldBucket(size+2), which gives 7 px for size 2 and 21 px for size 14.
- Reused deeper field (engine.ts:706), or headroom field (engine.ts:717-718): the band is as wide as that deeper field.
- Bevel has the same problem. In a pure-function test, inner bevel size 6 on 70% alpha shades 15 px with the bucket field and 3 px with a depth-30 field. Opaque content shades 8 px either way.
- The existing test "stroke and bevel give identical results from a deeper cached field" (review.test.ts:94) only uses binary mattes, so it misses this.

**The proposed fixes are not right**
- Reusing only fields of equal depth and dropping the headroom would make cached match fresh. But the widths stay wrong (7 px for size 2) and dragging the size loses field reuse.
- Using the requested maxDist in the soft-pixel bound has the same problem.
- Marking renders approximate (markApprox) makes exports match fresh but still wrong.

Severity stays major. A Stroke set to 2 px exports as 7-21 px depending on edit history, and the same happens with Bevel. The scope is inside/center Stroke and Bevel on content whose alpha is between 50% and 100% (soft-brush paint below 100% opacity, smoke and glow assets, feathered cut-outs, translucent text colours). Outside Stroke, the default position, is unaffected.
verdict.betterFix:
Fix the distance transform, not the cache. In src/render/distance.ts `envelope()` (lines 269-273), apply the own-coverage bound only to real anti-aliasing pixels, i.e. those whose nearest site is an 8-neighbour:

`if (d2 <= 2 && (outside ? a > 0 : a < 255)) { ... }`

A threshold of `d2 <= 4` also works and changes a few fewer opaque-AA pixels. Pixels deeper inside soft content then get true sub-pixel-corrected distances.

Why this works:
- Every value below maxDist becomes independent of the field depth. md2 is always greater than 16, so any small fixed threshold keeps that true.
- The cache-reuse rule `e.maxDist >= maxDist` and the drag headroom (engine.ts:706, 717-718) become valid as they stand.
- The widths come out right.
